ARASA has since grown to have a presence in 18 countries and now works in partnership with 115 Civil Society Organisations. ARASA is recognised in the region and internationally as a champion for Health rights and a strategic influencer and has its ear to the ground through its vast network of passionate and committed partners from diverse backgrounds and operational focus areas. Sida has traditonally been the main funder of ARASA. Others are UNDP, Pitch Funding, RCNC and Open Society Foundations among others. ARASA has applied to Sweden for SEK 41,273,614 funding to implement the 'AIDS and Rights Alliance for Southern Africa (ARASA) Regional Programme, 2019 - 2022 ' My Body is Not a Democracy'. The intervention aims at contributing to the removal of legal, policy and social barriers to the protection of the rights to bodily autonomy and integrity (BAI) for all and to achieve sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender and Intersex (LGBTI) persons, women, adolescent girls and young women and to ultimately achieve health, dignity and well being for sustainable development. Specifically, ARASA will work to eliminate stigma and discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, advocate for increased access to acceptable, quality and comprehensive SRHR services as part of the Universal Health Coverage. Will promote increased access to safe abortion for all women in all their diversity, and access to acceptable and quality HIV prevention servicesProposed activities will focus on: •Capacity strengthening and raising awareness for both civil society and key influencers and decision-makers, •Coalition building and engaging of new partneregional and national advocacy to influence policy development and law reform, •Creating spaces for horizontal learning and sharing of good practices for civil society and key influencers and decision-makers, and•Research and the generation of evidence for advocacy,Efficient and effective implementation of activities, are expected to deliver the following outcomes: - Civil societies with increased co-ordination, understanding, capacity, agency and strategic alliances, which will in turn contribute to stronger, more inclusive movements for SRHR and the use of acquired skills to mobilise communities for transformation of social norms and to advocate to national key influencers and decision makers for positive changes to laws, policies and financial allocations. - Key influencers and decision makers have increased understanding of the need to realise the rights to bodily autonomy and integrity and fulfil SRHR and of the impact of failure to do so on health and use this to catalyse positive changes to laws, policies and financial allocations. title: Building Capacity and Knowledge Exchange Pathways to understand how Climate Change affects Infectious and Non-Communicable Disease Prevalence in East
long_description: The World Bank, the World Health Organization and UNICEF have all warned around the need to better understand the harmful effects of climate change on health and disease, especially in low-and-middle-income-countries. Such effects can readily be seen, with Sub-Saharan Africa suffering some of the worst impacts. In Kenya, for example, recent record drought periods, followed by floods have led to food insecurity and limited access to clean water, resulting in increased cases of severe acute malnutrition in vulnerable populations as well as outbreaks of gastrointestinal infections like cholera.Our aim is to build knowledge exchange pathways/capabilities to develop appropriate digital tools/systems that will, in future, have the potential to be used in Sub-Saharan Africa to explore the local/regional links between disease prevalence and climate change. In preparation for this, we propose building a Frontiers Community, by holding a workshop focused on developing the appropriate collaborations and knowledge exchange pathways with key partners/stakeholders in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania, to build the cross-disciplinary relationships and show feasibility of how digital tools can be used to monitor these inter-dependencies.Key challenges around data inter-operability, data ownership and management as well as ethics/privacy will also be addressed through structured discussions during the workshop. In this context, as a key outcome of this award, we wish to de-risk future funding applications by demonstrating potential inter-operability across databases/data-formats, held by different stakeholders.As a near-term outcome after this workshop, we will show that the team has the capacity and capability to demonstrate that by integrating retrospective meteorological databases with historical healthcare data, we can identify regional associations between the prevalence of communicable/infectious disease (e.g. malaria/cholera), non-communicable disease (e.g. malnutrition) and climate change, at a local or regional level. In the longer term, such retrospective correlations will be used prospectively to help health boards make predictive interventions.'

title: COMMUNITY GRANT KENYA 1
long_description: The proposed project, titled 'Food Systems Dialogue leveraging Engineering for Climate Change Mitigation,' led by LIF alumni Irene, aims to address critical issues in Western Kenya's food systems through innovative and collaborative efforts. The project aligns seamlessly with the objectives of the LIF Community Grant Programme, focusing on building impactful networks, fostering collaboration, and positively influencing local communities.The central theme of the project is to bring together a diverse group of stakeholders from various sectors, including county government, banking institutions, research organizations, academia, food activists, and engineering associations. This collaborative effort is geared towards addressing the multifaceted challenges posed by climate change in the Western Kenya region, particularly within the context of food systems.The project's core components include a one-day 'Food Systems Dialogue' in Kisumu, drawing in 100 participants with expertise spanning county governance, finance, research, academia, activism, and engineering. This dynamic gathering will serve as a platform for innovative discussions, idea exchange, and problem-solving, with the overarching goal of leveraging engineering solutions to mitigate the impacts of climate change on local food systems. The engagement of stakeholders from multiple sectors is designed to foster cross-sectoral collaboration, echoing the LIF Community Grant Programme's emphasis on professional collaboration between alumni cohorts and diverse sectors.Irene's localized knowledge of the Agri Food SME landscape in western Kenya is a cornerstone of the project's success. Building on her previous experience in convening stakeholders for access to finance discussions, she understands the unique challenges faced by local businesses and aims to apply this knowledge to the broader context of climate change and food systems. This targeted approach ensures that the proposed project is not only relevant but deeply rooted in the specific needs and opportunities of the Western Kenya Region region.Anticipated outcomes include the establishment of new and qualitative business connections within the LIF network and beyond, with a focus on engineering-led solutions for climate-smart agriculture. The project aims to engage a significant number of LIF participants, encouraging them to take on leadership roles within their sectors and communities. This active participation aligns with the objective of developing communities of LIF alumni positively impacting local communities and enhancing the visibility of the LIF brand.'Food Systems Dialogue leveraging Engineering for Climate Change Mitigation' project is poised to make a substantial contribution to the development of the LIF alumni network. The project's potential to create lasting impact, foster cross-sectoral collaboration, and address critical challenges in Western Kenya's food systems aligns seamlessly with the overarching goals of the LIF Community Grant Programme. This initiative is not only an opportunity to drive positive change but also to elevate the visibility of the LIF brand in the Western Kenya Region.

title: Connect Rural Uganda - leaving noone behind in the Digital era - UNCDF - Connect Rural Uganda - UNCDF
long_description: The proposed contribution is called Connect Rural Uganda and is a five-year program, 2019-2024 (mid-2019 to mid- 2024) aiming to, through increased digitalization, empower rural communities with particular focus on refugees, women and girls, youths and smallholder farmers/agri-businesses. The target groups are of course overlapping. For market development small and medium sized enterprises is an important target group. The programme aims to reach vulnerable populations wherefor refugees and host communities in Northern Uganda are in focus, a region where a large majority is multidimesionally poor (and women and youth extremely vulnerable), where rights are being violated and where access to quality service is strained from the large influx of refugees in recent years. Despite the Ugandan Governments progressive refugee policy it is unlikely that the refugees will return to their countries of origin in the short /medium term. Therefore, programming of interventions must consider practical solutions towards integration within Uganda. The scoping of the program and the focus on the three sectors agriculture, education and health, builds on an analysis of current contextual challenges to rural development and assessment of key sector areas to which digital innovations and technology can be leveraged to unlock sustainable change in livelihoods in refugee areas. Examples of specified outcomes for the program are for example that farmers have improved access to information on agricultural management practices, markets and farming technologies, digital financial services, and power for farming practices. That agro-MSMEs have improved commodity distribution and marketing systems, and better access to credit. That schools have improved efficiencies in payment and monitoring systems, and access to quality teaching and learning materials. That rural populations have improved options for health payments and financing (savings, loans, insurance). And that new business models and technologies for delivering services are scaled for rural communities.The intervention targets refugees and host communities in Northern Uganda in the districts of Lira, Oyam, Dokolo, Alebtong, Masindi, Apac, Yumbe, Moyo, Arua, Adjumani, Nebbi, Zombo, Maracha. The geographic focus has been chosen with regards to its poverty levels (one of the poorest regions in Uganda), high vulnerability, lack of access to social services (e.g. health and education) and lack of inclusive economic development. But also with regards to the opportunities and market potential when it comes to introducing and scaling digital solutions to leverage development impact. Mobile technology offers important opportunities in this regard. Access to mobile technology has increased with drastic speed in Uganda. 53% of females and 71% of men owns a mobile phone (2016). Refugees tend to, more than the population at large, access mobile technology with the specific needs to communicate with family members in their home country or use it for financial transactions like remittances. Financial inclusion (including mobile transations) is many times a driver for people to secure access to a phone.

title: Developing Acute Care and Emergency Referral Systems(ACERS)
long_description: The Developing Acute Care and Emergency Referral Systems Project assesses the added value of a program of implementation research, action, and capacity building to timely care-seeking behavior and effective referrals to improve maternal and neonatal care in two regions of Ghana. Project efforts build off the Three Delay Model, with a focus on the second and third delay for obstetric and neonatal emergencies. Ghana continues to experience high maternal and neonatal mortality rates despite a well-organized, decentralized system of health care. Additionally, the lack of policies and guidelines for comprehensive care at the district level have resulted in emergency care and referral initiatives that are not well-coordinated and have unknown efficacy and impact. The ACERS project will augment the Community-based Health Planning and Services (CHPS) platform with activities around acute care and emergency referral systems from the community to the district level, seeking to prove that separate components of care can be assembled into a sustainable single system with scale-up capabilities. ACERS will be woven into the fabric of Ghana s regional, district, and community health system structures to ensure the implementation of a sustainable and scalable model. This implementation research effort, co-managed and co-financed by USAID Ghana, supports the Government of Ghana s vision of improved service delivery and progress towards self-reliance.

title: Evaluating fifteen-minute parks' improvements to the social determinants of urban health and wellbeing
long_description: Improved evidence is needed for decision makers from rapidly evolving cities in LMICs on the critical role that urban greenspaces can play as positive social determinants of health. Equity challenges mean existing greenspaces are often not widely accessible with those from marginalised groups least likely to receive their health benefits. We will assess a living case study of the Bangkok's Metropolitan Administration 101 15-minute pocket- parks initiative. Working closely and collaboratively with local communities and municipal agencies, findings will be used to shape the main rollout of the Bangkok parks, and more broadly inform applications of the pocket park model in other Global South cities for healthier populations. We will generate policy relevant evidence of the value and role of equitably distributed small-scale urban greenspaces on the SDH.

title: Fleming Fund – Commonwealth Partnerships for Antimicrobial Stewardship (CwPAMS)
long_description: This is an Official Development Assistance (ODA) funded UKaid project from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)'s Fleming Fund. The Fleming Fund helps to fight antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where the burden of drug-resistant infection is greater. This is a health partnership programme to improve antimicrobial stewardship across Zambia, Tanzania, Ghana, Uganda, Sierra Leone, Kenya, Malawi and Nigeria. The partnerships leverage the expertise of UK health institutions and technical experts to strengthen the capacity of the national health workforce and institutions in partner countries to address AMR challenges. The project aims to: (1) Develop partnerships between NHS Trusts (hospitals) and clinics/hospitals in LMIC Commonwealth countries, (2) Share UK expertise abroad as well as bring skills and knowledge back to NHS Trusts, (3) Create focused partnerships on the theme of AMR, that includes activity on: Antimicrobial stewardship, including surveillance (AMS), Infection prevention control, and antimicrobial pharmacy expertise and capacity, and (4) More generally improve the knowledge, skills and empowerment of healthcare professionals and pharmacists in partner institutions, thus enabling the healthcare workforce to ultimately contribute to a strengthened health system.

title: Fleming Fund – Country and Regional Grants and Fellowship Programme
long_description: This is an Official Development Assistance (ODA) funded UKaid project from the Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)'s Fleming Fund. The Fleming Fund helps to fight antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) where the burden of drug-resistant infection is greater. A management agent, Mott MacDonald, has been appointed to deliver: (1) Country grants across up to 25 LMICs, (2) Regional grants in West Africa, East and Southern Africa, South Asia and Southeast Asia, (3) Global projects, and (4) A fellowships programme. These initiatives aim to improve laboratory capacity and diagnosis, data generation and use, and strengthen AMR surveillance systems. Through the country, regional and strategic grants, and the fellowships programme the Fleming Fund will: (1) Build laboratory capacity for diagnosis, (2) Collect data on drug resistance, drug quality, drug use and the burden of disease associated with AMR, (3) Enable the sharing of data relevant to AMR locally, regionally, and internationally, (4) Encourage the application of data to promote the rational use of antimicrobials, (5) Shape a sustainable system for AMR surveillance and data sharing, and (5) Increase national leadership in addressing AMR.

title: Fleming Fund – GRAM Global Burden of Disease Project
long_description: Grant from the UK Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC)'s Fleming Fund to the University of Oxford, working in collaboration with the Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation, to strengthen the evidence base on the current global burden of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), and help us to understand how, where and why it is changing. The Global Research on Antimicrobial Resistance (GRAM) project is providing the essential health intelligence to help drive awareness, support better surveillance, and prompt policy action to control AMR, including facilitating antimicrobial stewardship. The Fleming Fund grant specifically supports the collection and synthesis of data on the burden of disease associated with AMR in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and is working to ensure that AMR is included within the Global Burden of Disease study. Projects funded through the Fleming Fund will benefit people in LMICs, where the burden of drug-resistant infection is greater.

title: Fleming Fund – Multilateral Grant to World Organisation for Animal Health (WOAH)

The strategy aligns with the Global Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance (GAP) through its four pillars: (1) Improved awareness and understanding, (2) Strengthened knowledge through surveillance and Research, (3) Support good governance and capacity building, and (4) Encourage implementation of international standards. The project strengthens coordination across the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), the World Health Organization (WHO), the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) and WOAH in supporting the One Health* agenda globally, specifically in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where the burden of drug-resistant infection is greater. (*One Health is an integrated, unifying approach that aims to sustainably balance and optimise the health of people, animals and ecosystems. It recognises that the health of humans, domestic and wild animals, plants, and the wider environment (including ecosystems) are closely linked and interdependent.)

title: Project support UNICEF in Ukraine and Moldova 2024-2026
long_description: Project support to UNICEF to strengthen the childcare system in Ukraine and Moldova and support the reform work towards family-based care. In Ukraina, the project is expected to strengthen the childcare system in 14 hromadas in Kharkiv and Volyn oblasts, benefitting 350,000 people, including 61,500 children. It will also strengthen the capacity of 3,260 social workers to respond to the needs of children. UNICEF will map existing capacities and needs in Ukraine and contribute to develop and scale up family-based care. UNICEF will support training of staff, repair buildings where social services are provided, and establish working groups in each oblast to contribute to the implementation of the so-called Better Care Reform on regional and local levels. UNICEF will also develop a framework to enable continuous training and capacity strengthening of social workers, including educational programmes, to contribute to sustainability over time. In Moldova, the project is expected to contribute to 45,000 children and 60,000 caregivers who have fled Ukraine or are otherwise in a vulnerable situation (e.g. children living in institutions) to receive support. It will also contribute to strengthening the capacity of 2,000 social workers. UNICEF will, similar to the work in Ukraine, map existing capacities and needs in Moldova, train staff, and contribute to developing and scaling up family-based care. Focus will also be on developing mobile services, including to strengthen the capacity to reach children with disabilities. UNICEF will also work to support young people in independent supervised living arrangements. Finally, financial support will be provided to vulnerable families. Sweden has positive experiences supporting UNICEF's humanitarian work in Ukraine and Moldova since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

Through early identification of environmental, social and economic sustainability risks associated with major investments, Business Sweden, in collaboration with Swedish development cooperation and export financing organizations, can assist with measures required for project owners to find financiers for the projects and ensure that sustainability criteria are taken into account in the procurements. title: Reimagining health-industry policy linkages in Africa for pandemic preparedness
long_description: The COVID-19 pandemic has exposed the risks and challenges of relying on imports and the global supply chains to satisfy the local healthcare needs in Low-Middle Income Countries (LMICs). Specifically, the pandemic exposed the lack of broad-based industrial capabilities in LMICs and missing links between health and industrial policies, creating serious questions about responding to the future pandemic. Our previous research has highlighted a need for supporting, strengthening and reimagining the health-industrial policy linkages to stimulate local industrial development through various routes such as agile regulation, innovative procurement, protected markets for local manufacturers, and incentivising technological upgrading. Focusing on Kenya and South Africa, this project engages with a critical question related to health-industrial policy linkages concerning pandemic preparedness: How can the policy be reimagined to support the development of local health-industrial linkages to create broad-based local industrial capabilities and thereby improve local health security for pandemic preparedness?

title: Support to Digital Reform in the Health Sector
long_description: Administration in Uzbek healthcare facilities is largely carried out in analog form. Patient records and communication within and between facilities are kept in paper form. Consequently, there is also a lack of robust data on key planning variables in the healthcare sector. This impedes evidence-based decision-making, sector management and demand-driven allocation of resources. Overall, the health care system is inefficient and error-prone. The Uzbek government has recognized the challenges, particularly with regard to financing, digitalization and service delivery, and has initiated ambitious reform plans. The implementation of digital reform in the health sector is based on a reform concept to which the FC feasibility study contributed significantly. Its integral components and a corresponding timeline are set out in a roadmap/digital strategy that serves as a guiding document. This module supports priority measures of the digital reform concept. Implementation of digital reform requires funding for comprehensive IT infrastructure, procurement of hardware and software, connection of public health facilities to high-speed Internet connections, and provision of a health information management system. The provision of an implementation consultant will support the implementation of the reform and promote the governance structure in the field of digital health. IT capacities will be strengthened as part of the accompanying measure.

The successful implementation of the UPEHSDP will help reduce child mortality and morbidity by reducing the prevalence of waterborne and food-related diseases, increase productivity by reducing overall morbidity, and improve the quality of life of urban inhabitants. UPEHSDP will improve the health status of the poor in urban areas and assist Bangladesh to make progress on the Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) relating to child and maternal health care and communicable diseases (MDGs 4, 5, and 6), and improve urban sanitation (MDG 7). title: 3D Slicer for African Scientists: Enabling AI for Health
long_description: Programme: Discretionary Award. Description: The 3D Slicer medical image computing platform is used in biomedical research worldwide. However, the development of 3D Slicer extensions is primarily designed for English. Additionally, the application lacks support for right- to-left languages like Arabic. Our proposed project will build infrastructure for developing 3D Slicer extensions in non-English languages and leverage customized Large Language Models (LLM) to simplify interface translation. Furthermore, we will organize events to support African developers in utilizing these new tools. This effort will empower researchers worldwide, especially in Africa, to build biomedical research tools for diseases afflicting local populations. For example, researchers in Senegal plan to develop AI-based 3D Slicer extensions to diagnose mycetoma, a disease endemic to poorer regions. The proposed project will enable them to develop a prototype extension for AI-based mycetoma diagnosis in French, and to utilize our LLM to distribute it to Arabic-speaking users. The project brings together medical imaging specialists, data scientists, and surgeons from the US, Senegal, Mauritania, and Canada. By empowering African scientists to create and distribute 3D Slicer extensions in any language, we aim to foster international collaboration and address global health challenges. Keywords: Artificial Intelligence, Open source software, Large Language Models, Mycetoma, Software Internationalization and Localization

The aim is to improve health care systems and the health situation of the population. The immediate target group is nurses and midwives. The beneficiary of the program is the EAC, the executing agency is the Aga Khan University (AKU). The aim of AKU is to train highly qualified nurses and midwives who will assume a leading position in their professional lives and serve as role models, be it in health care, in the field of education, in professional organizations or in health administration. The alumni are to act as multipliers, promote quality in the health care systems and also contribute to making the professional field of nurses and midwives more attractive. The measures of the FC program include the construction and renovation of two university buildings and a student dormitory as well as their equipment for nurse and midwife training (infrastructure component). Furthermore, existing vocational training programs are to be extended to rural areas, two new study programs are to be developed and established, and the implementation of targeted practice-oriented short training courses is to be expanded. Likewise a study financing program is to be conceived. A major result should also be the EAC-wide harmonization of study programs and degrees (academic component). The total costs of the project amount to EUR 27.2 million, of which the FC contribution (grant) is EUR 17.2 million from regional funds (EUR 10 million, commitment 2011 / EUR 7.2 million, commitment 2012 (VPT). The contribution of the AKU amounts to EUR 10 million.

title: An integrative approach to improve the management of snakebite envenoming in Latin America.
long_description: Programme: Discretionary Award. Description: Snakebite envenoming exerts a heavy toll in Latin America. Over decades, the region has undertaken relevant efforts to confront this neglected tropical disease through the production and distribution of antivenoms and training of public health staff in the diagnosis and management of envenoming, among other fields. Following up some regional projects carried out under the auspices of JICA, CYTED and the OAS, PANAFTOSA/PAHO established the Latin American Network of Public Antivenom Manufacturing Laboratories (RELAPA, Spanish acronym). RELAPA has implemented several initiatives to improve the regional landscape of antivenom manufacture and quality control and initiated activities to improve epidemiological health surveillance with the focal points in charge of snakebite envenoming at the ministries of health in the region, consolidating these concerted regional efforts in a manner fully aligned with the WHO strategy for the prevention and control of snakebite envenoming. The present proposal aims to foster a series of actions and to consolidate past and future efforts with the goal of strengthening RELAPA as regional network reference and platform for technical cooperation, by improving access to antivenoms, strengthening production and distribution capacities, access and improving clinical diagnosis and envenoming treatment, and the national epidemiological health surveillance programs in the region.

India Alliance has played a pivotal role in boosting research capacity through fellowships, attracting scientists to establish competitive research programmes in India and more recently, collaborative grants, addressing key public health challenges. title: GCWHI Incorporating a sex/gender lens in medical education in Pakistan
long_description: to incorporate a cross-cutting sex & gender lens into medical education in Pakistan, engaging leadership of Aga Khan University and Khyber Medical University and working in close collaboration with the Pakistan Medical and Dental Council

title: Global Health Protection Programme (BMG) - LabTrain
long_description: Strengthening Capacity and Structure Building in Drug Quality Assurance in African Countries ' A contribution of BfArM to WHO Standards and Good Laboratory Practice' (LabTrain). Project objective: To increase the overall capacity of African QCLs by enhancing the productivity and knowledge of laboratory staff and contributing to the development of the International Pharmacopoeia, Sub-objective 1: Support capacity and structure building of African QCLs for improved drug quality analysis, Sub-objective 2: Establish pharmacopoeial standards for the WHO International Pharmacopoeia The direct target group of the project are the employees and quality control laboratories of the national pharmaceutical authorities in the participating countries who are involved in the quality control of medicinal products.

title: Global programme: ITM Education and scholarships programme
long_description: The Education programme, part of the Global Programme for academic development cooperation of ITM, provides access to quality higher education in International / Global health and Global One Health, support for career development of alumni and staff at partner institutions and support for educational development for the latter. The Education Programme thus comprises a scholarship programme (for formal training and individual fellowships) and the Alliance project. The Alliance project focusses on lifelong learning including career support and on educational collaboration, its more individual and more institutional component respectively.In our Theory of Change (ToC), in tune with the ToC in the Joint Strategic Framework HES4SD, we hypothesize that access to international, interactive and interdisciplinary short courses, master programmes and doctoral training is both a demand and a need in our partner countries and beyond.We also hypothesize that the impact of training and ensuing knowledge production, will depend on increased agency for change of professionals and institutions (as drivers of change). The importance of lifelong learning and regional and international networking is not to be underestimated as pathways towards change and ultimately the contribution to better health (SDG3 through SDG4).The Education Programme is complementary to the 12 country programmes and concerned education initiatives at partner institutions. The education programme allows targeted training of additional human resources and support for internationalisation and innovation in education, be it through instructional design, development of technology enhanced learning or e.g. professionalisation of teaching staff. Equal access to the scholarship programme and alumni activities goes beyond country programmes. A truly Global Campus at ITM is paramount for the quality of interactive education, peer-learning, networking and fostering Global Citizenship. -

title: Health and Science Investment Cluster (PARES): Obstetric ultrasound training and research collaboration in obstetrics
long_description: Training gynaecology and obstetrics interns and some specialists in obstetric ultrasound and, in selected cases, basic invasive techniques.Collaboration with research projects in the area of Maternal Health that require studies of variables assessable by obstetric ultrasound (e.g. Doppler flowmetry, foetal biometry, foetal anatomical assessment).Increased response capacity in advanced obstetric ultrasound for the local population

title: Health and Science Investment Cluster (PARES): Strengthening Oral Health Systems and Professional Training in Guinea-Bissau and S. Tome and Principe
long_description: The overall aim of the project is to help improve the oral health conditions of the Guinean and São Toméan populations by strengthening public infrastructure in Guinea-Bissau and São Tomé and Príncipe with equipment, instruments and clinical consumables for oral health and by training local health professionals, with a view to more effective action by these professionals in the areas of health and the provision of health care to the most vulnerable populations in the regions of São Domingos and Catió (Guinea-Bissau) and Água Grande and Mé-Zochi (São Tomé and Príncipe).Project under the PARES program - Program to Support Health Response in Portuguese-speaking African Countries (PALOP)

title: Health Cluster and Investment in Science: PALOP EXPERTSAÚDE: Hospital Specialized Training Program
long_description: To contribute to the universal coverage of health services in the PALOP and to overcome geographical, economic or epidemiological barriers to access to health for specific groups.

title: Healthcare Personnel Training Program
long_description: The program provides medical personnel from partner countries with one to three months of on-the-job training, enhancing their knowledge and experience, and thereby improving the quality of health care in partner countries.

title: High-Level Regional Seminar on Promoting Cancer Awareness and Advocacy Program in the OIC Member States
long_description: The main objectives of the regional seminar are to (i) enhance awareness of the increasing cancer burden in OIC Member States especially in the sub-Saharan African region, (ii) share best practices and promote regional coordination mechanisms in cancer registry, cancer control planning and implementation to strengthen health systems, (iii) discuss ways of expanding access to effective cancer prevention, diagnosis, treatment and care, and (iv) identify ways and means through the First Ladies of the Member States within the region can further enhance their leadership role in effectively addressing the disease and saving lives.

title: House of Europe
long_description: the'' House of Europe'' will promote people-to-people contacts between the EU and Ukrainian society to share best practices and encourage mutual understanding

title: Improved health, protection, resilience of communities and ecosystems through One Health promotion
long_description: The outcome will ensure intersectoral collaboration and coordination among human, animal and environmental health professionals, as well as within communities, in mitigating health risks through improved preparedness for, and in response to, human and animal disease outbreaks. The outcome will increase food security and income for vulnerable households and preservation of ecosystems. The capacities of local partners and stakeholders will be reinforced and knowledge and lessons learned will be shared. The project aims at bringing together partners in the human health, animal health, and environmental health sectors to enhance safety, protection, resilience and create capacity to survey, monitor, diagnose and understand the drivers of disease at human-animal-environmental interfaces. The project will be implemented in the areas surrounding Nyungwe and Akagera National Parks in Nyaruguru and Nyamagabe districts in the southern province and Kayonza District in the eastern province. The project will be implemented in partnership with local organizations (IMBARAGA and ARDI) and in close synergy with the Belgian Red Cross and ADA. National institutions (local authorities, RAB, RCVD, MINAGRI, MINISANTE, RDB and academic institutions) as well as private institutions like SACCOs and Africans Parks are also key stakeholders. The main project activities range from NRM management activities, strengthening human/animal and environmental health services, establishing surveillance system to prevent health risks, enhancing community economic resilience and ensuring sustainable food production, strengthening CBO & CSO, and supporting service providers through access to credit and small grants. -

title: Improvement of the public health services in Dangkor District Referral Hospitlal
long_description: As a CPA2 level hospital, build a hospital, provide medical equipmen and conduct capacity building programs to strengthen the capabilities of Dangkor referral hospital, including establishment of guidelines and care system to enhance medical services.

title: Improving access to asthma care for children and adolescents in Uganda
long_description: MRC ARL award to understand whether innovations like checking every child and adolescent visiting primary care health facilities for asthma symptoms can lead to an increase in the number of children diagnosed with asthma, and whether education about asthma directed to patients and their caregivers can lead to improvements in the understanding of asthma, use of medicines and subsequent reduction in frequency of symptoms.

title: Improving access to primary health care in neglected areas in Southern Africa
long_description: Public health care in South Africa, Eswatini and Botswana is inadequate and leads to massive bottlenecks in remote regions and on the part of the vulnerable population. The aim is therefore to strengthen Catholic health services that ensure equal access to health care for vulnerable people. The work of the Catholic Health Network, which carries out training, information exchange and advocacy for Catholic health services, is financed. The target group is the staff of the network's member organisations. (LDC share)

title: Improving access to speech therapy services for Ukrainianchildren and empowering specialists working in educationalinstitutions
long_description: The goal of the SpeakTX project is to improve access to speech therapy for children withspeech disorders in Ukraine. During the project, a digital speech therapy platform withinteractive exercises will be localized, which speech therapists and parents can use tosupport children's language development.

title: Joint European Initiative to Strengthen the Medical Specialization in Ethiopia
long_description: The Joint European Initiative to Strengthen Medical Specialization in Ethiopia is a project of the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID), the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), and the European Union, in close collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health of Ethiopia (FMoH). The aim is to support the capacity of the Ethiopian Health System to recover from conflict and crisis, making it more resilient to future shocks.Objectives:The project focuses on three main areas of intervention, mostly mirroring the national Ethiopian Medical Specialization Programme.More specifically, the project seeks to: Improve human resources development in eight targeted hospitals, through specialized training.Improve infrastructure for specialized medicine and provision of quality and context-based equipment.Reinforce hospital management capacities identified as a gap by the Government.

title: Joint European Initiative to Strengthen the Medical Specialization in Ethiopia
long_description: The program aims at supporting the Ethiopian health sector in facing possible future shocks, through the strengthening of the medical specialization programs in 8 university hospitals. Specifically it focuses on the improvement of the medical specialties system through trainings held by European specialists, provision of equipment and small rehabilitations, trainings on management, researches.

title: Kiribati Institute of Technology - Facilities and Nursing Curriculum
long_description: This Activity will strengthen Kiribati Institute of Technology's capacity to offer high quality vocational education, through a modernised nursing curriculum and upgraded facilities. The facilities will be used for both medical and more general educational training.

title: KUHeS Strategic Partnership
long_description: Focused on SDGs 3 (Health) and 8 (Work): grant to University Of Glasgow to establish fully-equipped laboratories at the College of Medicine, Blantyre, enabling scientists there to conduct research into increasingly prevalent non-communicable diseases in Malawi, and working peer-peer research into NCDs with GU.

title: Live surgery: knowledge sharing and training
long_description: Increasing the quality of health care for children with a medical condition requiring surgery through improved training activities to benefit 60 medical students and pediatric surgery residents at Cheikh Anta Diop University in Dakar.

title: LUOHE MEDICAL COLLEGE EXPANSION
long_description: The Project comprises the expansion of Luohe Medical College into a new campus in Zhaoling District of Luohe City, with about 180,000 square meters of new buildings including the teaching building, a simulated training hospital, a library with information centre, a gymnasium and stadium, dormitories and dining halls for students, with internal roads, services, and landscaping works. The Project also includes consulting services for design, inspection and supervision of construction.

long_description: Quality Improvement on Medical and Nursing Education Improving medical educationo curriculum and evaluation system Improving nursing education curriculum Invitation training Design of clinical training for professors competency development Quality Improvement on Medical and Nursing Education Enhancing professors research capacity Structuring research support systemIndustrial Academic cooperation with enhanced capabilities

title: MF5-04 Paediatric Critical Care Capacity Building Project in Papua New Guinea
long_description: The Royal Australasian College of Surgeons (RACS) will work with their in-country partners The Papua New Guinea Women Doctors Association (PNG-WDA), The Pediatric Society of Papua New Guinea (PS-PNG) and the Advanced Pediatric Life Support Faculty Papua New Guinea (APLS-PNG) to contribute to improved health outcomes for pediatric patients across Papua New Guinea (PNG) by providing comprehensive clinical training courses and gender awareness training.

title: Mobility grants towards Developing Countries
long_description: A research grant has been assigned to a UNIVR Medical resident for a development cooperation project to be carried out in Brazil. title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange

The project will also consolidate their collaborative knowledge on workforce development for optometry programs. Kenya, Norway and South Africa

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: The main objective of the project is to improve the care of sick and premature newborns at the partner hospital in India. Through a digital education program combined with a practical learning though focus groups, the project aims to improve the service and care provided to newborns in the intensive care unit of the hospital. The project also aims to continue the management and development of the milk bank centre located at the hospital. The project has achieved very good results in the past. The aim to preserve the results achieved and to make them sustainable through the activities planned for 2022.

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: This project aims to strengthen the care of sick and premature neonates and support human milk banking in India. Furthermore, health personnel will be empowered in collaborative work in different cultural settings with diverging levels of resources and varying challenges. the latter will be aparticullar focus for the Norwegian partner OUS. There will also be a focus on teaching the teacher.This projects therefor seeks to ensure the delivery of essential new-born care providing vital attention to all infants during the crucial days following birth by improving the knowledge and skillset of nurses in the neonatal intensive care unit at LHMC & KSCH. NICU nurses coming to OUH get the opportunity to see the full spectrum of treatments and care, including several that are not yet fully implemented in India. Some of these treatments are planned to be introduced with help from OUH, during the next three years. The Indian exchange staff will be exposed to different routines, organization, and teamwork and more.

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: Through the exchange of health personell, the partners will work on improvement of leadership, ensure better use of medical technical equipment, improve the capacity of anaesthesia and neurosurgery, improve intensive care and neurosurgical care services, and improved care of paediatric surgical patients at the partner hospitals.

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: Through volume training and exchange of skills, the project aims to improve patient services in traumatology/emergency medicine. The project will improve communication and multidisciplinary cooperation between staff members at Accident & Emergency department. Furthermore, the project continues the digital cooperation between the two hospitals, which was established in the previous project.

title: Nursing Education & Specialization in Kvemo Kartli and Kakheti Regions - Geo Hospitals
long_description: Geo Hospitals LLC operates a network of 15 inpatient and 10 outpatient facilities across five regions of Georgia, employing over 1,350 doctors and 1,000 nurses. In collaboration with the USAID Industry-led Skills Program, Geo Hospitals is developing a sustainable postgraduate nursing education system in the Kvemo Kartli (Marneuli) and Kakheti (Sagarejo) regions. This initiative aims to replicate specialized training programs from Poland, adhering to EU standards, as a foundation for continuous nursing education in two new regional training centers. The focus will be on training specialties in high demand within the healthcare industry, specifically surgical, pediatric, and intensive care nursing. Over the long term, Geo Hospitals aims to train 320 nurses through this program. This private-sector-driven initiative addresses the critical shortage of qualified nursing staff in the country, particularly in rural areas. Geo Hospitals allocated and renovated training facilities in Marneuli and Sagarejo, conducted stakeholder meetings, and covered training-related costs, while USAID funded the development of training materials, procured equipment, and provided training of teachers.

title: Paraguay Disaster Response and Emergency Medical Service Capacity Enhancement Education Training Project ('23-'25)(2024)

The association improves the quality of teaching and helps secure pharmaceutical care in the country.

title: Portuguese Capacity Building Mission in Sao Tome and Principe (MPC-RD STP) - Support for the Development of the Armed Forces and Health Support
long_description: In the area of Health, the mission aimed to contribute to the development of the Health Training Plan, through an Advanced First Aid Course.In STP, the Military Health Education, Training and Research Unit (UEFISM) provided training to members of the STP Armed Forces and the Fire Department, based on the Advanced First Aid Course and the Immediate Life Support Course. This training is aimed at providing first aid in civilian and military settings and aims to develop skills in the following areas:- First aid to victims of an accident or sudden illness, until the arrival of pre-hospital emergency resources,- Operational first aid,- Health evacuation and transportation.

title: Project for establishment of National Rehabilitation center in Fiji
long_description: Newly built Fiji National Rehabilitation Centre, Provided equipment to improve diagnosis and treatment functions, Improved system of hospital operation and rehabilitation medical services, Well trained rehabilitation medical staffs

title: Project to Promote Regional Medical Cooperation System in Northeastern Cambodia through Strengthening Surgical Practice
long_description: This project aims at ensuring cooperation for surgery in Kratie province.?It will promote hospitals' ability to identify and refer patients and extend the capabilities and leadership of the Kratie Provincial Referral Hospital as a regional surgical hub.

title: Project to support the cultivating of speech-language therapists in Vietnam and to establish a center for the development of oral functions
long_description: This project will support the expansion of the educational system of the Graduate School of Dentistry, Hanoi Medical University. With request by the University, a center for the development of language and oral functions will be established.

title: Promote the health programs of the Aga Khan University
long_description: The objective of the FC project is to provide more and better trained health professionals by establishing and expanding a high-quality training and further training program in the EAC member states (FC program objective). The aim is to improve health care systems and the health situation of the population. The immediate target group is nurses and midwives. The beneficiary of the program is the EAC, the executing agency is the Aga Khan University (AKU). The aim of AKU is to train highly qualified nurses and midwives who will assume a leading position in their professional lives and serve as role models, be it in health care, in the field of education, in professional organizations or in health administration. The alumni are to act as multipliers, promote quality in the health care systems and also contribute to making the professional field of nurses and midwives more attractive. The measures of the FC program include the construction and renovation of two university buildings and a student dormitory as well as their equipment for nurse and midwife training (infrastructure component). Furthermore, existing vocational training programs are to be extended to rural areas, two new study programs are to be developed and established, and the implementation of targeted practice-oriented short training courses is to be expanded. Likewise a study financing program is to be conceived. A major result should also be the EAC-wide harmonization of study programs and degrees (academic component). The total costs of the project amount to EUR 27.2 million, of which the FC contribution (grant) is EUR 17.2 million from regional funds (EUR 10 million, commitment 2011 / EUR 7.2 million, commitment 2012 (VPT). The contribution of the AKU amounts to EUR 10 million.

title: Promoting holistic and inclusive developmental support in early childhood in Mongolia
long_description: The project will improve the physical environment and strengthen the capacity of local public service providers to enable early identification and intervention of disabilities in early childhood.

title: Promotion of nursing training in the Palestinian territories
long_description: Nursing training for women and men in the project region contributes to improving healthcare for the population. The target groups complete practice-oriented training in nursing with a focus on pediatrics, which offers them the prospect of an appropriately paid job in the health sector and improves their own living situation and that of their families. Through educational work, the attitude of the Palestinian population towards health and hygiene is changed for the better and is given greater consideration at various levels of society (family, educational institutions, social institutions).

title: Qualification of medical doctors in family medicine (continuation)
long_description: Subsidy of further study of physician specializing in family medicine, with practical training in rural hospitals and theory in Kinshasa, plus research, and lobbying government for good legal regulations for family medicine and good countrywide basic health service.

title: Quality and continuity of care: training of the nursing staff of the Simão Mendes National Hospital – Bissau
long_description: The training project aims to enhance and develop the skills of the nursing staff of the Hospital Nacional Simão Mendes (HNSM) in Bissau, in order to take care of the users' health problems effectively.

title: Raising health awareness in the society in Belarus
long_description: General aim of the project is to raise health awareness of the population of Belarus and to improve their health behaviour, hence three subactivities will be conducted by us. First of all we will train the lecturers of Belarus, so that they would instruct CPR with their students in local organisations. In Estonia we have a similar project 'Your Hands Save Lives, with our students and lecturers, which has decreased mortality caused by sudden deaths. Second subactivity teaches simulation methodology, which could be the basis for teaching in the classroom. Real life situations will be used, our topics are: clinical nursing, traumas, labour and intensive care. Third subactivity instructs the lecturers how to conduct an online course in English entitled 'Adult Health Behavior.

title: Regional Center of Excellence for Vaccines, Immunization and Health Supply Chain Management, Phase II
long_description: To unlock the development potential of the East African Community (EAC), improving the health status of the population is of great importance, for which efficient health systems are imperative. Currently, the EAC faces an acute shortage of sufficient numbers of well-trained healthcare workers at the national and regional health system levels, as well as at the district and health facility levels, who can adequately manage healthcare facility supply chains. The EAC therefore established a Regional Center of Excellence to strengthen these competencies in 2016, the Regional Center of Excellence for Vaccines Immunization and Health Supply Chain Management (RCE-VIHSCM). The RCE-VIHSCM is based in Kigali at the University of Rwanda, School of Public Health (UR/SPH) and offers academic and short-term training courses both in Kigali and in the other EAC member states through its regional network The objective of the FC project is to further expand the high-quality education and training offered in health logistics in the EAC and to further establish the RCE-VIHSCM as a focal point in the region for the introduction and dissemination of innovation and best practices. To achieve these goals, investment measures supported by KfW are required for the further equipment of the center of excellence (e.g. IT, cold chain lab), as well as the financing of scholarships, the expansion of the training program and research, and measures for the further development of the center into a regional consulting center. The total costs amount to approximately EUR 15.95 million, of which EUR 14.0 million will be financed through FC grant funds and approximately EUR 1.95 million will be contributed by the University of Rwanda/ School of Public Health (project executing agency).

title: Regional Center of Excellence for Vaccines, Immunization and Health Supply Chain Management
long_description: Strong health systems are vital to improve the health status of the people in For unfolding the East African Community's (EAC) and allowing them to further unfold the region's potential for continued development. An essential component of health care is good supply chain management, i.e. an adequate management for supply of health centers with medical products. This includes vaccines, diagnostic tests, drugs, medical devices and family planning. Currently, the EAC suffers from an acute lack of employees with professional training in supply chain management at the in national, regional and district level as well as at health centers. Therefore, the EAC strive to establish a Regional Center of Excellence to strengthen these competences. The aim of the project is to support the development of a high-quality training program, including a master's degree program and further qualification courses in health supply chain management in the EAC and to create a regional hub for expertise in supply chain management that can support the introduction of innovation within the region. The Centre of Excellence contributes to the goals of the new initiative for Africa of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development and German six-point-plan. Investments shall be made in infrastructure, scholarships and the establishment of the training program as well as start-up funding for the operationalization of the Centre. The overall costs for establishing the Regional Centre of Excellence amount to approximately 11,14 million euros, whereof 10 million euros shall be funded through Financial Cooperation.

title: Rehabilitation Training Program for Ukrainian Healthcare Workers
long_description: The goal of the project is to conduct team-based rehabilitation training for Ukrainian healthcare workers. The training program will provide a theoretical and practical overview of contemporary multidisciplinary rehabilitation principles. The focus within this project will be on the rehabilitation of the patients with lower limb amputations.

title: Renforcement de l'école de formation en soins infirmiers d'Attapeu
long_description: KoGe is an umbrella organization whose mandate is aligned with the SDG 16+ framework (peaceful, just and inclusive societies). With its faith-based member organizations of protestant background that are deeply anchored in the Swiss society, KoGe empowers disadvantaged people and provides access to food security, education and health. It also strengthens communities in peacebuilding and conflict transformation.

title: Royal Australasian College of Surgeons 2024 - 2029
long_description: The ANCP is a unique Australian aid program. It is a partnership between the Australian Government and accredited Australian NGOs. For 50 years, this partnership has contributed to sustainable economic growth and poverty reduction in some of the world's poorest countries. The ANCP is the Australian Government's longest running and largest NGO program.

title: Sages-femmes pour Parbatipur
long_description: The GEH Alliance promotes gender equality, engages with most vulnerable groups for their sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), takes action to prevent sexual and gender-based violence (SGBV) and provides support to survivors. It includes men and boys in transformative processes of unequal gender relations and the prevention of SGBV. In 19 countries with partly very fragile contexts, the alliance promotes inclusive access to mother-child health through targeted policy dialogue and the strengthening of local health systems.

title: Scotland Malawi Mental Health Project (SMMHEP)
long_description: Building on two previous Scottish Government grants that established Malawi's first ever M.Med Psychiatry, it will provide funding for four trainees to become clinically qualified psychiatrists at Malawi's College of Medicine. Trainees will undertake two years' training at the College of Medicine and two years' specialist tuition at the University of Cape Town. The trainees will be supported by e-learning materials previously created under a University of Edinburgh project funded by the Scottish Government.

title: Securing orthopedic care and training local specialists Queen of Universe Hospital in Puma, Tanzania
long_description: Patients with hip, knee and joint arthrosis do not find adequate care in Tanzania. Planned with a focus on SDG-1, 2 1. the development of training documents and optimization of the training rooms as well as the training of specialists in the treatment of osteoarthritis patients

title: SolidarInvest
long_description: The EdM-SM Alliance stands for equal access to quality health services and education adapted to local socio-economic realities. The Alliance works with vulnerable and most disadvantaged groups: women, children and poor people, mainly in rural areas. Thematic priorities are the strengthening of health and education systems, community-based approaches in mother-child health as well as primary education. The Alliance works on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, (Non-) Communicable Diseases and on social determinants of health.

title: Strengthening capacities in Lviv Territorial Medical Union and Rehabilitation Centre Unbroken
long_description: The project aim is to contribute to improving the quality and efficiency of health care in Ukraine. The goal of the project is to strengthen the professional and material capacity of the Lviv Territorial Medical Union (LTMU) and the National rehabilitation center Unbroken at the level of primary and specialised health care. To achieve the goal, the following outputs will be targeted: 1. Development of guidelines for antibiotic therapy management, 2. Development of guidelines for the burn treatment, 3.Strengthening the professional capacity of rehabilitation workers, The project is implemented by the Czech Health Technology Institute, z.s., a non-profit organization that contributes to the development and export of new innovative technologies in the field of health care, supports and provides educational programs and supports humanitarian aid abroad. To facilitate the expert medical part of the project, it cooperates with the 1st Faculty of Medicine of the Charles University and General Teaching Hospital Prague, especially in providing training for pharmacists and general practitioners, and rehabilitation workers. Burn treatment area will be coordinated with the Teaching Hospital Brno. 1st Faculty of Medicine of Charles University guarantees the expert cooperation in overall.

title: STRENGTHENING THE OROTTA HOSPITAL IN ASMARA - REHABILITATION OF THE CARDIOVASCULAR INTENSIVE CARE UNIT AND MEDICAL TRAINING
long_description: The bilateral initiative STRENGTHENING OF OROTTA HOSPITAL IN ASMARA - REHABILITATION PROJECT FOR THE CARDIOVASCULAR INTENSIVE CARE UNIT AND MEDICAL TRAINING aims to establish and launch a Cardiology Intensive Care Unit (CICU) at Orotta Hospital in Asmara, Eritrea. The objective is to enhance the management of cardiac conditions and contribute to reducing mortality related to coronary diseases. Simultaneously, the initiative includes the following i) Providing highly specialized training activities to specialized healthcare personnel in Eritrea at various professional levels for cardiac pathologies, ii) Supplying medical equipment for the operating room, sterilization room, and intensive care unit, iii) Providing medicines, consumables, and biomedical supplies for cardiovascular pathologies.

title: Support for oncological rehabilitation and war-affected patients
long_description: The project will focus on rehabilitation for community of patients with oncology in Ukraine by addressing critical gaps in equipment, inclusive spaces within the hospital, professional skills, and patient care at the National Cancer Institute. Additionally, personalized rehabilitation sessions and psychological support will be offered to 200 patients, including 70 children, to improve physical recovery and mental well-being. This intervention will strengthen Ukraine's rehabilitation services, ensuring better access to quality health care for those most affected by war and illness. The project is implemented in cooperation with Zaporuka NGO in total value of 5 000 000,- CZK

title: Support of education and promotion of biomedical engineering in Cambodia
long_description: The University of Health Sciences (UHS) and the Institute of Technology (ITC) have established a new degree programme Associate degree in Medical Engineering. The first students of this programme are already completing their studies to become biomedical engineers, however, the limited number of teachers, experience and lack of laboratory equipment still does not allow to implement the teaching fully. At the same time, the general public and hospital staff have no awareness of the biomedical engineering profession and do not know how important this profession is to the health care system. The intention of this project is therefore mainly to: 1. to increase the number of youth and adults who have the relevant skills and knowledge, including technical and professional skills, which will be a prerequisite for gaining decent employment, by educating lecturers and students of UHS and ITC, providing equipment for practical training and providing educational materials, 2. to inform the society and improve its awareness of the position of the biomedical engineer and his/her role and importance by organizing an international conference, creating promotional and advertising materials and establishing a website on biomedical engineering, 3. To raise the level of the Associate Degree in Medical Engineering program by opening a special laboratory to enable practical teaching of subjects on medical devices and by training lecturers in this field, and at the same time to help to prepare documents for accreditation of the programme from Associate to Bachelor and to implement biomedical engineering position in the job tables of the state health system.

title: Training of medical professionals of BiH in modern procedures for treating traumatic injuries - study visit, expert trip, material donation (sdc)
long_description: The aim of the project, led by the Medical facility of the Ministry of the Interior of the Czech Republic, was to train members and paramedics of the Federal Civil Protection Administration (FUCZ) in modern procedures and means of treating traumatic injuries according to the principles of Tactical First Aid in a Civilian Environment. These are paramedics who cooperate with deminers on demining and disposal of unexploded ordnance, while encountering traumatic injuries and their procedures and set standards no longer correspond to the modern concept of trauma medicine. Participants were introduced to current medical devices and materials used in the treatment of a traumatically injured patient (e.g. tourniquets, hemostatic gauze, chest valves, drains, decompression needles and other sophisticated material). The project focused on theory as well as practice. As part of the project, a material donation was also made. These were 3 fully equipped backpacks with medical supplies, which should serve as an example for Bosnian colleagues of the standard equipment they should have at their disposal in their activities. title: Unravelling the mechanisms of neurological damage during cryptococcal infection of the brain
long_description: MRC ARL award, Cryptococcal meningitis kills more than 200,000 people each year in Sub-Saharan Africa and also causes neurological dysfunction and disability in survivors, most of which are of an economically productive age. Cryptococcal meningitis (CM) is the leading cause of HIV-associated meningitis, which is characterised by debilitating, inflammatory injury of the brain and a very high chance of death, even with treatment. In Sub-Saharan Africa, the number of people who die from CM and its complications is worsened by the unavailability and inaccessibility of safe and effective drugs. This research will fill the existing knowledge gap on how the brain is injured in cryptococcal meningitis. This models and methods would then serve as a platform for studying the mechanisms of other infections of the Central Nervous System that are caused by bacteria, parasites and viruses to inform the development of the much-needed new therapies in South Africa and the wider Sub-Saharan Africa region.

title: 2nd Global Summit on Diamond Open Access
long_description: Programme: Discretionary Award. Description: The global summit in Toluca (Mexico) has cleared the uncertainty for the need to consolidate the assertion that research output is a public good. Global south countries, in serious efforts to find solutions to its challenges to share its research output, have embraced and grown diamond open access. For this summit there is cognition and support for more to be done to mainstream diamond open access. Further this summit set to affirm the rejection of APCs. Further, there is a realization by funders that their support for APCs is not sustainable and they are now throwing their weight behind diamond open access, in particular, the financial components (the cost factor). After a very successful summit, it is expedient that another global south region pursues the continuation of conversations and the consolidation of diamond open access. The summit in Cape Town is intended to make explicit that financial barriers, for authors, are not the only challenge that has to be navigated to get published. The summit will, amongst others, unpack diamond open access through a social justice lens. One of the foci is the development of a publishing ecosystem that is devoid of bias, both conscious and unconscious.

title: A 'safe systems' approach for enabling traffic injury prevention in Nepal (SAFETrIP Nepal)
long_description: This programme of research aims to improve collaboration between health and other agencies to reduce road traffic deaths and injuries in Nepal.It is being conducted through a collaboration between the University of the West of England, Bristol UK and Kathmandu Medical College, Kathmandu, Nepal, together with, Safe and Sustainable Travel Nepal (a charity advocating for safer travel in Nepal), MIRA (a non-governmental organisation in Nepal that supports research), emergency care experts in Nepal and colleagues at Imperial College London.This research is important because road traffic injuries are the 12th most common cause of death globally, and the leading cause of death in 5-29 year olds. Approximately 1.3 million people die and over 50 million people are injured in road traffic crashes each year, with over 90% of victims being from low- and middle-income countries. Nepal, a low-income country, has recently had a big road-building programme and there has been a large increase in vehicle ownership. However, without good road safety leadership, coordination and funding, the number of road traffic injuries have increased and there is no national ambulance service to provide prehospital care to those injured. Road traffic injuries are one of the most preventable causes of death, injury and disability. A 'Safe Systems' approach, in which all agencies work together to create an environment which keeps road users safe, has been shown to lead to significant reductions in rates of road traffic injuries.Between 01/11/2022 and 31/10/2026 we will conduct three work packages that will support the development of a safe road system in Nepal and will map to two of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, 3.6 (halve global road traffic deaths and injuries) and 11.2 (provide access to safe, affordable, accessible and sustainable transport systems for all, and improving road safety). The work packages focus on: (1) Supporting leadership and action for road safety at local and provincial government levels, (2) Strengthening public transport safety (specifically bus travel), and (3) Improving the care of those with injuries following a traffic crash. A fourth work package will improve researcher's awareness of how to keep research data safe whilst still maximising its use.

They are at 1.94 times higher risk of developing dementia and need to receive prompt intervention. In Thailand, this population is equal to over 20 million older adults. Hearing evaluation and screening needs not only advanced medical equipment but also well-trained medical personnel such as audiologists, audiovestibular medicine physicians etc., which Thailand lacks. However, over 90% of older adults in Thailand can access mobile phones and applications. Using remote mobile technology can help not only create affordable hearing screening health but also increase accessibility for older adults in remote areas. We partner with an industrial partner who received the TSP funding in 2021 with advanced software and mobile application technology in both Android and iOS systems to conduct hearing screening and evaluation.Main outputs of this project 1. Evaluate the AI algorithm of the mobile application to conduct hearing testing without human supervision.The result with be compared with medical-personnel lead standard testing environment2. Access the acceptability of Thai older adults/community in using the mobile hearing screening application.The community in Thailand suburbs will use the application to self-test their hearing. The acceptability of the application in the community will be explored.3. title: Behavioural Determinants of Multimorbidity in Malawi
long_description: Programme: PhD Studentship for Health Professionals. Description: Malawi has a high, and rising, prevalence of multimorbidity - the co- occurrence of two or more long-term conditions - as it undergoes a demographic and epidemiological transition from a predominantly young, rural population to an increasingly urban and older population. Many common long-term conditions share proximate causes, including physical activity, sedentary behaviour, and sleep, which together can be described as 24-hour free living movement behaviour. While these are well described in studies from high-income settings, much less is known about the relationship between 24-hour free living movement behaviour and multimorbidity in a low-income setting such as Malawi, where physical activity is more likely to be occupational or travel- related rather than a leisure-time activity. This study will examine the relationship between 24-hour free living movement behaviours and multimorbidity, through the collection of accelerometer data from 4000 participants evenly divided across an urban (Area 25, Lilongwe) and a rural (Chilumba, Karonga) site in Malawi. This data will be linked to demographic, health, and anthropometric data from a larger Long Term Conditions survey, in which this study will be nested, in order to assess the association between these behaviours and multimorbidity.

title: Birthing at Burning Places: An ethnographic exploration of intersections among climate-linked risks, maternal nutritional health, and cultural practices in Sindh Pakistan
long_description: Programme: Wellcome Accelerator Awards. Description: Extreme weather and natural disasters contribute to a wide range of health, food, and nutritional risks, particularly in low—and middle-income countries such as Pakistan. Women are the largest and most vulnerable unduly groups of victims who suffer the most from such disasters. Pregnancy and childbirth exacerbate these vulnerabilities further. The health of mothers is not just a healthcare issue. It is deeply connected to power imbalances, cultural norms, and practices. Similarly, the environmental changes we are witnessing raise important questions about the relationship between nature and culture. Gender dynamics, social class, and cultural norms significantly affect pregnant women and mothers' ability to access, use, and manage food and nutrition. These dynamics also contribute to the disproportionate impact of climate change events on women's health. Given that maternal health-related targets in Pakistan are falling short of the Sustainable Development Goals, research providing an in-depth understanding of intersectional influences on maternal health, nutrition and climate change is urgently needed to inform the development of interventions to enhance women's and families' health and wellbeing. This project aims to co-produce community-based solutions to improve maternal nutritional health by exploring the intersections between maternal nutritional health, cultural practices, and climate-related risks through ethnographic research.

title: C-it DU-it: Community Data Use for Integrated ANC
long_description: Timeline: 4 years (Oct 2022 – Sep 2026)Location: 4 counties in western Kenya (Homa Bay, Migori, Kisumu, Kakamega).Partners:• LVCT Health - the Lead Agency• Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI) – Collaborator• Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine (LSTM) – Collaborator• GinD - CollaboratorThis research project aims to strengthen community health systems in Kenya by increasing antenatal care (ANC) uptake through a health systems strengthening approach. The approach will link digital data platforms and train community Work Improvement Teams (WITs) to use the data they collect to identify problems and develop local solutions. The project entails 'seeing' linked data (C-it) and 'doing' or acting on the data (DU-it). The study seeks to answer the question, What is the effect of 'C-it DU it' on community health systems strengthening and what is required for effective transfer and scale-up?The project will enable smooth integration of data collected at both facility and community levels to track individuals from the community to facilities and back again. The study will pilot in Homa Bay County so as to introduce C-IT DU-it and increase the number of pregnant women achieving eight scheduled ANC contacts with a healthcare provider. The project will, from year 3, be scaled-up to the other three Kenyan Counties as an ideal way of transferring lessons.The project will use mixed methods implementation research design with four components:a) Realist evaluation will generate, empirically test and refine a transferrable programme theory to understand the causal relationship between context, participant response and outcomes.b) A 3-arm, cluster-randomised controlled trial in Homa Bay County will determine the efficacy of 'C-it' and 'C-it DU-it' to increase ANC contacts when compared to the standard of care.c) Health economic evaluation and equity analysis will compare health expenditure of women accessing and engaging with ANC care and determine costs and cost-effectiveness of C-it Du-it from a health systems perspective.d) Qualitative interviews will assess transferability and iterative scale-up of C-it DU-it across the three remaining counties using toolkits developed in Homa Bay.
