title: Supporting Mozambiques NAP Readiness Capacity
long_description: The goal of this proposed NAP Readiness Project is to establish a resilient and inclusive national adaptation planning ecosystem in Mozambique, enabling transformational, long-term shifts towards climate resilience. This framework will integrate climate adaptation into national, regional, and sectoral development planning, strengthen institutional capacities and mobilize sustainable financing for prioritized climate actionsTo combat pressing climate challenges, Mozambique has formulated a series of strategic policies that prioritize resilience and adaptation across vulnerable sectors.. Together, these policies establish a comprehensive approach to enhance Mozambique's adaptive capacity and align with international climate commitments:1.National Strategy for Adaptation and Mitigation of Climate Change (ENAMMC), 2013-2025: 2.National Adaptation Plan (NAP): 3.Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC)In analyzing Mozambique's adaptation framework key barriers that hinder cohesive, scalable climate change adaptation and resilience efforts:1.Limited governance and institutional coordination2.Deficient planning processes and technical capacity: effective climate adaptation requires robust planning processes, which Mozambique currently lacks, especially at the sub-national level. 3.Limited and inconsistent climate data:Mozambique faces data discrepancies between ministries, gaps in historical climate data and limited capacity for generating downscaled, sector-specific climate information. 4.Low stakeholder knowledge, engagement and awareness: In Mozambique, awareness and engagement levels are low, with limited involvement from local communities and private entities. 5.Limited private sector involvement and financing6.Lack of a holistic and inclusive adaptation approach 7.Inadequate financial resources and budgeting for adaptation: Mozambique's budget constraints limit its capacity to allocate adequate resources for adaptation.

title: The offroad vehicle of hope: project to supply an offroad vehicle for the Analaroa dispensary.
long_description: In Madagascar, the health service is private, a condition that prevents those who do not have sufficient economic resources from accessing care. In addition to widespread poverty and the extreme lack of health and social services, Madagascar is characterized by very critical road conditions. Most of the roads to the inland villages are dirt and impassable unless with suitable vehicles (offroad vehicles). Objective: to guarantee access to the villages and the provision of aid, in this specific case of a health nature. Activities: purchase of an offroad vehicle, replacing an old vehicle purchased about ten years ago, again with regional funds. Having a vehicle that is technically adequate for the conditions of the territory would allow the association and local health personnel to meet the care needs of the population that gravitates towards the hospital facilities of Analaroa and Anivorano, built by the Association itself. Sustainability factors: consolidated collaborative relationship between the association and the local partner (SuoreOrsoline FMI to guarantee correct use and maintenance, supervision by the association's staff in conjunction with onsite visits. Risk factors: probable rapid deterioration of the vehicle due to the precarious condition of the slopes.

long_description: The Trauma Rehabilitation for Ukraine (TRUE) project strengthens Ukraine's rehabilitation system to respond to the surge in war-related injuries and long-term disabilities. title: Wellcome Discretionary Award - Coalition for Mental Health Investment (CMHI
long_description: Programme: Discretionary Award. Description: African Venture Philanthropy Alliance (AVPA) respectfully requests GBP75,000 amount over 15 months to support the Coalition for Mental Health Investment (CMHI), in partnership with Kokoro Change, Wellcome, the Clinton Global Initiative and McKinsey Health Institute. Together, CMHI organizing partners will accelerate current efforts, galvanize additional partners and contributions, and deliver results and impact on both the implementation and financing sides of the mental health equation. This funding will enable AVPA to hire and equip 1 staff member to serve as a liaison with CMHI partners, and lead the delivery of work agreed through CMHI. Through its involvement in CMHI, AVPA will: • Provide expertise in innovative financing mechanisms based on track record and active engagement of mechanisms in health and other sectors • Support in providing access to a network of investors, experts, and implementors across Africa and, where feasible, other geographic markets, that could be relevant to progress CMHI's vision and objectives • Lead on incorporating mental health into AVPA's catalytic pooled funds and / or other innovative financing mechanisms as relevant • Offer space to highlight mental health investment issues and opportunities as well as CMHI at relevant regional and sub-regional conferences and events.

title: WHO, EMTCC Sudan response 2024
long_description: Following a call for international assistance by the MoH Sudan in May 2024 due to escalating healthcare needs, the Emergency Medical Teams Coordination Cell (EMTCC) in Sudan was activated in July 2024. The EMTCC, hosted by the WHO, addresses critical gaps in Sudan's health response by overseeing the deployment and coordination of Emergency Medical Teams (EMTs) across the country. The core purpose of an EMT Coordination Cell is to ensure that the overall response of EMTs (both National and International) best meet the excess healthcare needs that are a result of the emergency.

title: 2ª Fase: Ensuring the right to prenatal, maternal, child and infant health – including adequate levels of nutrition – in Uvinza DC District (Kigoma, T
long_description: 2ª Fase: This proposal aims to improve the exercise of the human right to quality sexual, reproductive, maternal and child health and nutrition in one of the eight districts of the Kigoma region: Uvinza DC. This intervention is part of the development and health programs that the Spanish Red Cross and the Tanzanian Red Cross have been implementing in the Kigoma region since 2015.Through a strategy based on 3 results, covering both the institutional health and community spheres, this proposal aims to contribute to guaranteeing the right to quality health for 72,444 rights-holders. The intervention aims to guarantee comprehensive and sustainable sexual and reproductive health services, adapted to gender and age, with cultural relevance, without discrimination and guaranteeing equality, access to information and the direct participation of the community in decision-making. Strengthening maternal-child and sexual and reproductive health facilities and services, developing the capacities of medical personnel and promoting healthy habits together with access to accurate information will help communities in the Uvinza DC district to improve their right to health.'

title: 2ª Fase: Promoting the right to health in Guinea Bissau with special attention to children with functional diversity
long_description: 2ª Fase: In the current context of the country, there are large groups of the population whose fundamental right to health protection and healthcare is violated. In this sense, the objective of the project is to promote the effective exercise of the human right to health in the Autonomous Sector of Bissau (SAB) and the specialized care of children with functional diversity through the achievement of four main results: the promotion of access to information on the right to health by citizens (Title of rights), that citizens receive social and legal support from the Patient Defense Office (ODP), specialized in cases of people at risk of social exclusion (Title of rights), the strengthening of Civil Society Organizations (OSC) to promote the effective exercise of the right to health (Title of Responsibilities), and the improvement of comprehensive health care for children with functional diversity at the Childhood Rehabilitation and Development Center (CRDC, by its acronym in Portuguese). These results will have a very positive impact on rights holders, who will be supported to know and exercise their rights to public services and basic health goods, as well as on the Ministry of Public Health (MINSAP) of Guinea Bissau, duty bearers, to exercise their role as guarantors of the rights to public services and basic goods for the entire population under the principles of equity and diversity. This will be possible thanks to the joint work with Liga Guineense dos Direitos Humanos (LGDH) and AIDA Guiné Bissau (AIDA GB), two local reference organizations in the country in the fields of human rights and health, our local partners and duty bearers.With this intervention, we will continue AIDA's work in Guinea Bissau in the field of health and continue to contribute to the achievement of Sustainable Development Goal 3: Ensure healthy lives and promote well-being at all ages.'

title: Act to End Neglected Tropical Diseases - East
long_description: Act to End NTDs East builds on the successes achieved through previous Agency investments to expand and strengthen national integrated NTD programs to achieve the WHO 2020 NTD goals. This five-year award, managed by RTI International, is intended to support disease-endemic countries to control and/or eliminate NTDs with proven, cost-effective public health interventions to treat and measure treatment impact against seven NTDs: lymphatic filariasis, blinding trachoma, onchocerciasis, schistosomiasis, and three intestinal worms known as soil-transmitted helminths. In addition to continued support toward global disease elimination and control goals, Act to End NTDs East will focus on helping countries on their journey to self-reliance by supporting them to integrate NTD programs into the broader national health systems and to strengthen technical, operation and financial capacity to operate NTD programs without U.S. foreign assistance funding. This centrally managed agreement will support Bangladesh, DRC, Ethiopia, Haiti, Indonesia, Laos, Mozambique, Nepal, Nigeria, Philippines, Tanzania, Uganda, and Vietnam.

title: Addressing Health Threats in Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Countries and the Caucasus
long_description: This knowledge and support technical assistance (TA) will enhance regional health cooperation in the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (CAREC) countries and the Caucasus. It will facilitate regional policy dialogues, knowledge sharing, and a more coordinated approach to common health threats and challenges. In particular, the TA will (i) develop innovative solutions in response to the ongoing coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic, and (ii) build capacity to jointly prevent, prepare for, and respond to regional health threats. The TA is a timely response to the COVID-19 crisis and likely future health threats, and builds on existing networks and projects in the region, addressing one of the main weaknesses––sectoral and institutional fragmentation and uncoordinated approaches.

title: C.A.R.E.S. - COMMUNITY ADVOCACY AND RESILIENT MOBILE CARE SERVICES
long_description: In Ukraine, Kosovo and Bosnia and Herzegovina, older people, especially women and people with disabilities, are affected by great poverty and isolation: the state health and social systems do not provide adequate care. The war post-war context and high inflation further exacerbate these challenges. Gender-specific role expectations mean that women usually bear the main burden of paid and unpaid care work. This can lead to overload and impaired quality of care. Professional and gender-sensitive mobile care services and psychosocial support are offered to vulnerable groups (older women, people with disabilities) living in urban and remote areas. Relevant stakeholders in the care sector (care and health staff, authorities, informal carers, ...) receive relevant gender-specific training on specific topics such as dementia, violence in care, medical emergencies at home, etc. Mobile care services are strengthened through intensive socio-political and advocacy work and supported by key interest groups.

title: CAMEROON: POSSIBILITY, WELCOME, CITIZENS, LISTENING
long_description: The project intervenes in the hardship phenomena caused by internal wars, which every year lead thousands of displaced people to pour into large cities, such as Douala, without means and without any support network. With the project actions we want to give assistance to these people who are forced to live in precarious situations, guests of families who have welcomed them but having very few means at their disposal. Assistance is also provided from a health point of view, informing them and accompanying them to carry out basic visits. It would be important to be able to give them the opportunity to carry out short training courses to introduce themselves into work paths: tailoring, IT, the hospitality sector, cooking. Small trades that can especially help women and adolescents, thus preventing them from ending up on the street and offering a chance to reenter working and social life. Another strand of intervention concerns orphanages, where it will contribute to the support of structures that can have high quality standards to guarantee autonomously and free of charge food, lodging, education, school and professional education, health care, and will also contribute to the creation of a serene and exemplary living environment, based on universally shared human values, and finally, as many children as possible will be given the opportunity to have access to adequate means and resources.

title: CSF 10-22 Y3 PAYMENT - Delivery of sustainable and quality eye health care at
long_description: To reduce the prevalence of avoidable blindness and visual impairment due to trachoma, cataract and refractive error (RE) in GGDKA-D in Ethiopia. These three leading causes of avoidable blindness in Ethiopia disproportionately affect rural women, girls, children and the elderly. Investment and interventions, supported by Irish Aid and Orbis Ireland, have reduced active and blinding trachoma prevalence, in fact 26% of targeted intervention districts are now below the World Health Organisation's (WHO) recommended cut-off levels. The project will continue to successfully implement the WHO's SAFE strategy (Surgery, Antibiotics, Facial cleanliness and Environmental improvement) by building on best practices and lessons learned since 2007.

title: CUDDLE: Caregivers' Upskilling and Digital Development Learning Empowerment
long_description: The goal of the project is to develop an online-based educational program, which aims at improving the professional skills as well as digital literacy of formal and informal caregivers in the Republic of Moldova and Germany. In the long term, this will improve the quality of home care and care for children, the elderly and people with disabilities, strengthen the social sector in the Danube region and promote international cooperation between the countries of the region. The project aims at developing a low-threshold, professional and modular basic qualification based on European health certificates and frameworks. During the funding period, it will develop, implement, and evaluate two pilot modules considering national specifics. It has a preliminary character: the overarching goal is the broad implementation of the teaching and learning program in further partner countries. Target groups are people with low qualification levels, family caregivers without professional expertise, people interested working in the care sector, as well as women in and after their family phase in both countries.

title: DCDC Dialysis Network
long_description: The transaction involves (i) an equity investment of up to $5,000,000 in Indian rupee equivalent, and (ii) the administration of an equity investment of up to $5,000,000 in Indian rupees equivalent, to be provided by the Leading Asia's Private Infrastructure Fund (LEAP), in DCDC Health Services Private Limited (DCDCPL) for the DCDC Dialysis Network Project in India and Sri Lanka. The equity investment will help DCDCPL expand its operations from the current 82 centers with 428 dialysis machines (all in India) to 136 centers with 1,438 dialysis machines in India and 45 centers with 900 dialysis machines in Sri Lanka. title: Developing Innovative Community-Based Long-Term Care Systems and Services
long_description: The knowledge and support technical assistance (TA) will build on the findings, recommendations, and lessons learned from TA 9111: Strengthening Developing Member Countries' (DMCs) Capacity in Elderly Care, approved in May 2016 and expected to be completed in May 2020. TA 9111 aimed to develop DMC capacity to adapt to aging populations and develop long-term care (LTC) systems and services. The country diagnostic studies conducted under the TA in six countries (Indonesia, Mongolia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tonga, and Viet Nam) have revealed large deficits in LTC services, especially those providing affordable and quality care. In each country, developing community-based services has emerged as a priority. This TA will (i) continue to build the knowledge base on LTC, (ii) develop innovative and sustainable community-based LTC service models that can operate in low income settings, deliver quality and affordable services, are sustainable and have potential for replication and, (iii) strengthen knowledge sharing and networking on LTC in the region. The TA seeks to create new partnerships for service delivery and to address the multiple care needs of older persons in Indonesia, Mongolia, Sri Lanka, and Viet Nam. The TA is included in the management-approved 2019 results-based work plan of the Sustainable Development and Climate Change Department. It is aligned with the Asian Development Bank's (ADB) Strategy 2030, particularly operational priority one?s agenda of addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities among the region's most vulnerable populations. The proposed community-based care models will support the development of technical assistance and lending portfolios on adapting to aging.

title: Development of health products and services network

These would otherwise be difficult to access. The company wants to expand in Uganda and Kenya to achieve economies of scale and build a commercial business case. In Uganda and Kenya, a ?last-mile? distribution network of around 4,000 CHEs, serving around 1 million families with affordable products and services, has already been established. Because health services are offered closer to home, families save a lot of money on transport costs. The combination of an efficient supply chain, the use of customer-friendly technology and the cooperation with local health entrepreneurs lead to significant improvement in the rural healthcare service. The company's goal is to expand to 16,400 CHEs in Uganda and Kenya in 2025 and to serve 3,8 million families. DGGF?s loan will support the company with their goals. The loan finances, among other things, health product supplies, prefinancing of CHEs product baskets, office costs, transport costs, selection and training costs, and tablets.

long_description: On its first ever mission, the neurosurgical team from Na Homolce Hospital performed 28 operations over five days on patients from the most vulnerable community segments of the population who had been waiting for surgery for several years. These included mainly health stabilization and trauma in the lumbar and cervical spine, as well as benign tumors.Contributes to TEI PHI (Public health institutes).

title: MEDEVAC mission Zambia in otorhinolaryngology. TEI
long_description: A team of ENT specialists from Motol Hospital completed their second health mission in Zambia, this time operating in four rooms at once. In cooperation with Zambian colleagues, Czech medical professionals managed to operate on a total of 43 patients with chronic otitis media, nasal polyps, nasal sinus tumors, salivary gland carcinomas, larynx carcinomas, and thyroid pathologies.Contributes to TEI PHI (Public health institutes).

title: MEDEVAC reconnaissance mission infectology
long_description: In April, a MEDEVAC reconnaissance mission was conducted at Vinnyky Hospital and St. Panteleimon Hospital in Lviv, led by MUDr. Petr Smejkal, an infectologist and hospital epidemiologist, head of the Department of Hygiene and Epidemiology at IKEM. The main goal of the mission was the health prevention and treatment of infectious complications of operations (prevention of surgical wound infections). Another goal was the implementation of rational antibiotic administration, in an effort to at least slightly reduce extreme antibiotic resistance in Ukraine.

title: MEDEVAC reconnaissance mission Zambia in neonatology. TEI
long_description: Following a request from the Zambian side, a reconnaissance in the field of neonatology took place in the Zambian Women and Newborn Hospital. Two doctors from Motol Hospital had the opportunity to visit all parts of the local neonatology department, including delivery and operating rooms, over the course of two days. Based on this reconnaissance, the MEDEVAC program plans to expand its health cooperation in Zambia to include neonatology, especially in the form of training and education.Contributes to TEI PHI (Public health institutes).

title: MEDEVAC reconnaissance mission Zambia in paediatric cardiac surgery. TEI
long_description: An additional reconnaissance mission of pediatric cardiac surgery took place in Zambia from 26 February to 1 March 2024, due to the higher demands and complexity of the planned first mission in this health specialization. A team of specialists from the Children's Cardiology Center of the Motol University Hospital assessed the readiness of the local hospital, in particular its material, hygiene environment and technical equipment, on site. Following the positive evaluation, the first mission took place in June.Contributes to TEI PHI (Public health institutes).

title: Medical Mission Lviv - Plastic and Reconstructive Surgery
long_description: The first medical mission of 2024 took place in April, when, under the auspices of the Kralovske Vinohrady University Hospital surgeons Prof. MUDr. Bretislav Lipovy, Ph.D., MBA, LL.M., doc. MUDr. Tomas Kempny, MUDr. Jakub Holoubek, Ph.D., and MUDr. Tomas Votruba set off for Lviv, Ukraine. Over the course of ten days, an experienced team of reconstructive surgeons operated on a total of 27 patients, with most of the operated injuries having a direct connection to the war conflict in Ukraine. The mission has direct influence on education of local expert community in the field of health.

title: Meeting The Challenge Of Urban PHC Systems – A Learning Sites Approach
long_description: To strengthen Maternal, Newborn Child Health, Maternal, Infant and Young Child Nutrition and Infectious Diseases prevention and service delivery strategies in selected states (Orissa, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka) of India.

title: MF5-05 Menstrual health management for girls/women with disabilities in Vanuatu
long_description: Reemi Charitable Trust will work with World Vision Vanuatu to reach individuals from the age of menarche and above with intellectual and physical disabilities in Vanuatu to manage menstruation by providing access to education and reusable menstrual materials. The Activity will also deliver a Menstrual Health Management outreach programme, aimed at improving the awareness of caregivers and families to support girls and women with disabilities during menstruation.

title: microsurgery & surgical accesses to the head – postgraduate workshop , Department of Macroscopy and Clinical Anatomy, Medical University of Graz
long_description: From 15-19 January 2024, a course for Ukrainian surgeons from the SUPERHUMANS Centre, Lviv, Ukraine, took place at the Institute of Macroscopic and Clinical Anatomy, Gottfried Schatz Research Centre at the Medical University of Graz, under the direction of Univ-Prof. Dr. Niels Hammer. During this week, university professors of Graz Medical University and their teams of experts provided their Ukrainian colleagues with insights into microsurgery and surgical approaches. The event was supported by the BMSGPK in cooperation with the OeAD Ukraine Office Austria, the Austrian Embassy Kyiv and the Austrian Association of Cities and Towns.

title: Miscellaneous Disease-related and Inter-disease Focuses
long_description: ViVac - Assessing trust in vaccination in conflict areas: Evidence-based data on the link between exposure to violence and health-seeking behaviors in Nigeria - Subproject Hamburg University - Research funding/knowledge transfer/advanced training/capacity building in education and research in developing country

title: MNCNH Rapid Commodity Market Diagnostic for Ethiopia, Kenya, and Nigeria
long_description: to develop a multi-country and multi-year market database for all MNCNH commodities for use as a baseline assessment for the MNCNH Innovation Accelerator and to inform country-level procurement practices and improve commodity availability

title: Mobile Therapy Unit
long_description: Ensure home rehabilitation for children and young people with various forms of disability who cannot/are unable to access specialized day care centres. To achieve small but significant daily autonomy that allows them to access specialized day care centres, schools for children and young people with special needs or be enrolled in local schools.

title: Modernization of Oblast medical Multiprofile Centers III (Accompanying Measure)
long_description: The objective is to improve the quality, efficiency and sustainability of medical care in the multi-profile centers at the regional level in the program regions. This is to be achieved by modernizing the medical equipment, introducing modern care methods, implementing rationalization and optimization measures as well as structural rehabilitation according to efficiency criteria. This is intended to contribute to the DC program objective of improving the health of the population as a whole. Subject to Uzbekistan's approval, the investment locations will include up to three additional multi-profile centers: Ferghanskaya oblast (city of Ferghana), Khoremskaya oblast (city of Urgench) and Yizzakskaya oblast (city of Yizzak). The target group of the program is the adult population of Uzbekistan. A total of around 7.6 million people live in the currently prioritized programme regions, of which around 6.0 million are adults. The total costs of the program are estimated at EUR 21.25 million, of which EUR 9.0 million are to be financed by FC funds and approx. EUR 12.25 million by Uzbekistan's own contribution.

title: Modification of contract between Chemonics International Inc. and Africa Global Logistics Zambia Ltd to provide in-kind donation of insecticide treated bed-net (ITN) warehouse storage
long_description: The parties agreed to extend the period of performance of the IQS fromDecember 15, 2023, to 29 February 2024 with no ceiling increase. It was agreed that AGL will provide thesame level of service and all existing contract terms for additional months at no charge (equivalent to $965,000 in-kind donation)

title: Multi-Methods Data Collection Mandate to Monitor the Swiss Cooperation Programme Zimbabwe Zambia 2023-2026
long_description: The purpose of this mandate is to support data collection for the monitoring and evaluation of Swiss supported projects in Zambia and Zimbabwe. The annual data collection and analysis will capture the perceptions of SDC project target groups around supported interventions in health service delivery, social protection, youth employment, agriculture, and good governance. This will help to see the trend or change of the different indicators of the Cooperation Programme.

title: Multisectoral Lifesaving Assistance, Yemen
long_description: The project will improve access to essential health and nutrition services and provide safe and clean water for conflict-affected communities in areas where humanitarian actors have limited access. It will rehabilitate and support health facilities and medical personnel and construct water supply networks for IDPs, local communities, and returnees. In total, the project will directly help 8,030 of the most affected people.

title: Mães e filhos Ingoré
long_description: The project involves the purchase of furniture and equipment to make the Giovanni Merlini Nutritional Center in Ingoré, a building that has recently undergone structural redevelopment, usable. Equipping the Center with new furnishings and equipment will finally make it possible to welcome patients and the health personnel necessary for the care of young women and their children in safety. The project proposal is aimed at promoting sustainable human development, through actions aimed at promoting health, reducing the phenomena of malnutrition and disparities in maternal and child health.

title: Nairobi County Performance Management
long_description: To support the Nairobi City County Government's health agenda focusing on strengthening accountability systems across PHC facilities to ensure service readiness.

title: National coordination of the network for health and nutrition in ten dioceses of Haiti
long_description: It contributes to improving the health status of vulnerable people by strengthening, structuring and making available basic health services throughout the country and reaching more patients.

title: NGO Volunteers in Dominican Republic for Basic health care
long_description: The WFK KOICA-NGO Volunteer Program dispatches volunteers to projects led by NGOs and other private sector initiatives abroad. In collaboration with KOICA and NGOs, volunteers are assigned to support and implement the NGOs projects in the partner countries, contributing to their economic and social development.

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: Based in poor regions of Bangladesh and Nepal, the two organisations work with health care of poor women and children. Through the project, the partners aim to share knowledge from one country to another to enhance their capacity within this field. The focus of the project is to improved maternal and neonatal health care, through improved nutrition and structures related to this. Bangladesh, Nepal.

title: Norway First Loss - FASA
long_description: USAID RFS to launch a new first-loss facility that will support commercial lending to agricultural small and medium enterprises (agri-SMEs) in Sub-Saharan Africa through Delegated Cooperation Arrangement (DCAR) donor-to-donor agreement with the Government of Norway.

title: NP Perinatal MCH
long_description: The program of the Terre des hommes Foundation (TdhF) aims to sustainably reduce child mortality and morbidity and to secure access to health, sanitation and clean water for mothers and children (0-18 years) in severe poverty. Children in contexts of migration, conflict and disasters, and child victims of violence are better protected. International standards in child-friendly justice are promoted. Humanitarian interventions in fragile contexts, combined with poverty reduction and sustainable development are promoted through innovative work with children and youths.

title: OMCUCA, emmergency Support for Internally Displaced Elederly in Adigrat
long_description: Psychosocial and Basic Needs Support for Elderly People of all religions in Adigrat, Tigray - support for those suffering from conflict traums, loniless and poverty

title: Optimizing Rwanda digital CHW program & generate evidence [Resolve]
long_description: To support Rwanda Ministry of Health to optimize their digital community health worker program and evaluate impact of the initiative.

title: Optimizing Rwanda digital CHW program for scale & generate evidence
long_description: To support Rwanda Ministry of Health to optimize their digital community health worker program and evaluate impact of the initiative.

title: OVC and Bright Futures/Colgate-Palmolive
long_description: To collaborate with Colgate - Palmolive, one of the private sector allies of OVC, through the initiative 'Bright Smiles, Bright Futures' program - which contribute with the provision of social services and donations for the benefit of the vulnerable families that are part of the Project.

title: Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) - Support
long_description: PMRS works for the attainment of physical, mental and social wellbeing of Palestinians. Health is viewed as an entry point for social change and community development.The Palestinian Medical Relief Society (PMRS) is a grassroots community-based Palestinian health organisation. PMRS seeks to improve the overall physical, mental, and social well being of all Palestinians, regardless of racial, political, social, economic status, religion or gender. The quality health services focus on the needs of the most vulnerable members of Palestinian society: women, children, disabled and the poor in rural villages, refugee camps, and urban centres. PMRS works to contribute to the building of a viable Palestinian civil society that contributes to the achievement of the national goal based on social equity, democracy, respect for human rights, a society that is free from discrimination and aggression of any form.Multi-year frame work agreement from 2018 till end of 2020. Annual payments (non-binding) were made prior to that.

title: Paths on the net: the DREAM mobile desk to guarantee information and accessibility to services to the resident population
long_description: Enabling the activation of a socialhealth mobile helpdesk service aimed at the population (isolated communities of Mererani), through the purchase of 4X4 car for outreach activities, awareness campaigns and education sessions sanitation in the Arusha Region

title: Performance-based partnership scheme focusing on quality programming, understanding change and results for poor households and communities
long_description: The A Healthy Future - Health and WASH System Strengthening and Community Action for Improved Child and Maternal Health and Nutrition programme will work in Centre-East Region, Kouritenga Province, Burkina Faso. It aims to contribute to Concern Burkina Faso's Health, Nutrition and WASH thematic programme, and the goal of the grant is to improve maternal, neonatal and child health and nutritional status by improving access to quality essential services, household resilience and promoting sustainable behaviour change. The programme will support over 1,351,200 people living in extreme and poor households, including internally displaced people particular focus on women and children under five. This will be done through strengthened community health management committees that empower women and the extreme poor, tailored support and advocacy provided to address bottlenecks and gaps in delivery of essential child medical and nutrition supplies the 'last mile' to health facilities and increased health, nutrition sanitation and hygiene awareness and the reduction of adoption barriers facilitating sustainable behaviour change.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Transitioning toward self sustainable food and health systems in Western CAR. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: DRR 1: Through system strengthening, the programme is strengthening the resilience of the heath system.Capacity Building 1: Training and capacity building was provided to community volunteers on WASH and awareness raising campaigns were held on healt, nutrition and WASH topics. Gender Equality 2: this is the main objective of the outcome, which is aimed at as it focus on reducing barriers and increasing access of women to basic health and nutrition services. RMNC Health 1: The aim of this programme is to improve child and maternal health and nutritional status by improving access to essential health, nutrition, water, sanitation and hygiene services and by promoting sustainable behaviour change for optimal feeding, caring and hygiene for children under-five and their carers. The primary target groups are children under-five and women of reproductive age, particularly pregnant women.Nutrition 1: Improving the nutrition status of women and children through improved nutrition awareness among communities is a focus of this outcome.

long_description: The A Healthy Future - Health and WASH System Strengthening and Community Action for Improved Child and Maternal Health and Nutrition programme will work in Centre-East Region, Kouritenga Province, Burkina Faso. title: Performance-based partnership scheme focusing on quality programming, understanding change and results for poor households and communities
long_description: The programme in Niger helps to improve access to basic needs and the rights to life, access to food, water, shelter and medical assistance for vulnerable people affected by humanitarian crises in 35 communities in Ouallam, Mirriah and Gouré in Niger. In 2024, GOAL directly reached 40,052 people in various sectors. Thanks to this programme, women's empowerment and decision-making are improved within communities through income-generating activities (VSLA). Access to basic healthcare is improved for people, particularly women and children, in areas where access to sanitation facilities is difficult. The programme supports vulnerable households and people with disabilities affected by multiple shocks. In addition, the programme provides access to smart farming techniques adapted to climate change in rural communities to improve diversification and consumption of a variety of micronutrient-rich foods.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 2: People Have Resilient Health. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: GOAL focuses on health system strengthening with the objective of increasing the number and percentage of health facilities providing quality health services (including nutrition services and WASH facilities), so that health and well-being can improve. Under the RMNCHN component, GOAL's intervention primarily aims to improve the health of pregnant and lactating women and adolescent girls, infants and children, and will also build the resilience of the health system.

title: Performance-based partnership scheme focusing on quality programming, understanding change and results for poor households and communities
long_description: Through ICSP in South Sudan, GOAL supports the health system in Abyei, Central Equatoria, Upper Nile and Warrap to provide services to vulnerable communities with a special focus on women, adolescents and children. The programme also supports women and youth who are the most impacted by crises to participate in economic development of the country through livelihood opportunities. Gender equity and social inclusion are at the centre of the programming to ensure disadvantaged groups are accommodated. In 2024, ICSP improved the lives of 543,188 vulnerable individuals in South Sudan.. OVERALL COUNTRY PROG: Outcome 2: People Have Resilient Health. SPECIFIC OUTCOME: Building resilience to shocks that impact health, such as disease outbreaks through a focus on Early Warning and Response Systems (EWRS) by working in collaboration with the Ministry of Health.

title: PIF Kenia: Upgrading Maternal and Newborn Care Units at 20 sites in Kenya
long_description: The project, implemented by the Kenyan Ministry of Health and VAMED Health Projects Finland Oy, will modernize the maternal and new-born units of 20 public health facilities across 12 counties in Kenya. This will include the construction and/or refurbishment of the departments, the supply and installation of medical equipment, and the provision of a wide range of training services and maintenance. The overall goal is the provision of better quality health services for pregnant women and new-borns. This will enable patients to seek professional pre-natal and post-natal health care in the renovated and newly equipped facilities, and shall increase the number of health check-ups of pregnant women..

title: Planning grant for scaling up azithromycin MDA in Mali and Niger
long_description: to develop costed country plans for the scale-up of mass treatment with azithromycin in Mali and Niger, and to strengthen a regional REACH network to share implementation experience and evidence to inform scale-up across the region

title: Playing with care
long_description: The project involves the creation of spaces equipped for safe recreational and play activities for children in the city of Beit Jala.

title: PMU for Supply Chain Funders Forum & Interagency Supply Group (ISG)
long_description: to build a strong model for global Procurement and Supply Chain collaboration that helps ensure key stakeholders are aligned on a shared vision and high impact priorities and positioned to drive progress against global goals

title: Pre-clinical PD for Lung Surfactant
long_description: to explore appropriate dosing of lung surfactant in order to reduce the dose as much as possible to enable LMIC procurement

title: Preparedness and Response (P&R) project
long_description: The goal of the Preparedness and Response (P&R) project is to enable national governments to establish and strengthen systems, policies, and practices for prevention, detection, response, and control of emerging disease threats - especially zoonotic diseases.

title: Presbyterian Health Services
long_description: Supporting local health activities and facilities by contributing to a fund established to cover the medical expenses of patients without health insurance.

title: Presbyterian Health Services
long_description: Supporting local health activities and institutions, through the contribution to a fund intended to cover the medical expenses of patients who do not have health insurance.

title: Preventing child marriage and adolescent pregnancy and supporting young mothers at CLF high school.
long_description: CLF in Iceland will implement a project aimed to reduce child marriage and adolescent pregnancy and to support young mothers at CLF high school. The main objective of the project is to reduce the risk of child marriage and adolescent pregnancy in Mukono district by equipping vulnerable adolescent girls with knowledge, skills and opportunities that allow them to make informed decisions about their lives and bodies, including if and when to get married or have children. The project will enhance education at the CLF school for both girls and boys, establish a health care centre based on the needs of youth and young mothers, expand the school to be able to host a higher number of students coming from challenging circumstances, support girls from difficult circumstances to return to school and to determine if and when they get married.

title: Program to Strengthen Integrated and Comprehensive Health Services Networks based on Primary Health Care
long_description: The overall objective of the program is to help improve the health conditions of Paraguay's most vulnerable population by strengthening the Comprehensive, Integrated Health Services Networks (RIISS) based on primary care. The specific objectives are to: (i) expand and strengthen the care network, and (ii) boost the quality of priority lines of care, including mother and child health, essential obstetrics and neonatal care, particularly diabetes, hypertension, and cancer, and HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis.

title: Program to Strengthen the Institutional Healthcare Service Network (PRORISS)
long_description: The objective of the program is to help reduce maternal and child mortality primarily in the departments of Huehuetenango and San Marcos, by modernizing the national healthcare network so it can deliver timely, quality, and efficient services.

title: Project Building Resilience- Multiple donors
long_description: To mobilize resources and goods from multiple entities including the private sector to improve the lives of extremely vulnerable communities through increase of access of health services, nutrition and economic stability

title: Projet de santé Biswas Népal
long_description: FAIRMED and Christoffel Blindenmission (CBM) have joined forces in the LNOB Alliance. It works in fragile contexts, prioritizing the needs of the most marginalized and discriminated people especially of women, men, girls and boys with disabilities. It seeks to improve living conditions of individuals and empowering marginalized communities while also strengthening inclusive systems and services. The Alliance contributes to the implementation of the UN Conventions on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, which Switzerland ratified in 2014.

title: Projet Marsabit LovE - Projet d'autonomisation des personnes malvoyantes à Marsabit (Low Vision 2.0) - KE

title: Promoting access to holistic palliative care for marginalized populations in nine states of India
long_description: Only 2% of patients in India have access to palliative care and pain relief. The aim of the project is to improve access to holistic medical and psycho-social palliative care for marginalized populations in selected regions of India. This is done through inpatient as well as decentralized care with hands-on palliative care nurses, involving family members and volunteers, and advocacy with government agencies.

title: Promoting basic health work in the health centers of the Assemblées Chrétiennes au Tchad, continuation
long_description: The project contributes to realising the best possible health care in the included regions. It builds on diverse experiences. Due to the quality of its services, the executing agency has become a reference hospital with state recognition and increasingly plays an important role in the local and national context for improved access to medical services.

title: Promoting health and combating poverty in the rural area of Mabaya
long_description: Strengthening the maternal and child health services of the Kanyaka Health Center by hiring a nurse to support the staff and the medicine supply.

title: Promoting holistic and sustainable healthcare in South Sudan
long_description: The healthcare system in South Sudan is largely dysfunctional due to a lack of state involvement. The project aims to enable three healthcare facilities to provide good quality healthcare services for the people in their catchment area. Personnel costs, in particular for medical staff, and running costs such as trainings are financed. In addition, the management of the health coordination will be further developed. The project's target group is particularly women (pregnant women) and children (under 5 years of age).

title: Promotion of community-based health work in eleven districts of a federal state in India
long_description: The project implementing partner organisation is committed to promoting healthcare in India. Through its cooperation with over fifty member institutions, it is not only active in improving the health situation by providing its own health care services in fourteen districts of one federal state, but also through targeted lobbying and advocacy work the implenting organisation calls for government commitment and an improvement in the quality of public health services especially for the marginalised target groups.

title: Promotion of home care in Armenia
long_description: The country program Promotion of Home Care in Armenia supports the current reform efforts in the field of elderly care. The aim is to anchor home care services in Armenia's health and social system to enable patient-oriented and efficient care, close an important care gap between inpatient and family-based care and strengthen the quality of care through competition among care service providers. At the same time, state actors, civil society and the public will be sensitized to the importance of health care and healthy and active ageing.

title: Provision of Health Care and Water Services for Saada IDPs in Razih District
long_description: Providing primary healthcare services including injury and bandaging treatments, safe disposal of waste and medical waste, as well as emergency health services and water to the displaced people of Saada Governorate. in addition to saving and preserving lives, reducing the spread of diseases and epidemics, and ensuring the well-being of those in need.

title: Psycho-social counselling for women with experience of Gender based violence, continuation.
long_description: In the project, medical staff in state and church health centres and hospitals are trained to provide appropriate medical care for survivors of sexualised violence and to interact with them in a stress- and trauma-sensitive manner. Furthermore, survivors are accompanied holistically, that includes medical, legal, psychosocial and economic accompaniment. The civil society is sensitised and encouraged to stand up against sexualised violence and for the rights of survivors using the forum theatre method.

title: Psycho-social health for families, continuation
long_description: The project offers crisis intervention, consultation and therapy for patients or groups of patients suffering from psychological disorders. It also implements preventive and capacity building measures for professionals with a medical, social or pedagogical background.

title: Psychosocial and medical care and public relations work for survivors of sexualized violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
long_description: The violent attacks on the civilian population and the expulsions in eastern Congo continue to lead to countless cases of sexualized violence against women and children, including in the provincial capital of Goma. The aim is therefore to strengthen medical and therapeutic counseling and support for survivors. Medical-therapeutic services and preventive measures are financed, such as occupational therapy measures and further training and training events for local authorities and local leaders on positive masculinity and combating gender-based violence. The target group is traumatized survivors

title: RDCongo Goma Coordination
long_description: Médecins Sans Frontières Suisse (MSF-CH) delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics &amp, disasters and to communities excluded from health services. It focuses on medical and surgical assistance as well as on strengthening of local healthcare. MSF-CH cares for mothers &amp, children, provides sexual, reproductive &amp, paediatric care, responds to epidemics such as Covid-19, and treats non-communicable diseases &amp, mental health conditions. It brings to attention neglected crises and advocates for improved medical treatments and protocols.

title: REACH Regional Dashboard
long_description: This investment aims to develop a tool(s) to systematically report on the progress, effectiveness, and impact of Resiliency through Azithromycin for Children (REACH) across implementation geographies.

title: Recovery and valorisation of medicinal and aromatic plants for healthcare enhancement in Morocco.
long_description: Help the rural community of the Eastern Region of Morocco improve the availability and quality of medical plants for the creation of effective phytotherapeutic health remedies accessible to all. a) Preserve and enhance, through the purchase and installation of a drying cell, endemic aromatic and medicinal plants, representative of the Eastern Region of Morocco, maximizing the content of bioactive substances contained in them. b) Generate knowledge and improve the knowhow of the foreign partner, through the purchase and installation of a galenic laboratory, for conscious and sustainable exploitation of plants and the delivery of training courses.

title: Regional project for Crisis Response in Earthquake-Affected Areas in Syria and Türkiye
long_description: Initial SituationOn 6 February 2023, earthquakes with a magnitude of up to 7.8 struck northern Syria and south-eastern Türkiye, causing widespread devastation. The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UN OCHA) estimates that around 15.7 million people in the region have been directly affected by the earthquakes. The tremors also destroyed or damaged more than four million buildings. According to official figures, around 59,000 people died.The current crisis response efforts are insufficient and are mainly focused on short-term results. Approaches which build resilience and capacities at local level, and which consider, in particular, women and marginalised people in all their diversity, are still lacking. The resilience of the population, especially women, is low in the context of crisis management.ObjectiveIn selected earthquake-affected areas in Syria and Türkiye, the resilience of the population - especially women - has been increased so that people can better deal with crises.ApproachThe project focuses on three key fields of action in its work to empower the population to deal with the impacts of the earthquakes:- It improves access to education and health services by rehabilitating damaged infrastructure. In addition, staff in education and health are trained to improve the quality of services.- It provides support to households affected by the earthquake by giving them access to financial services. Furthermore, small businesses are receiving micro-credits. In addition, skills development measures are being carried out, in particular for women.- It promotes crisis management in communities. So-called first responders are empowered to act appropriately and collectively in the event of future earthquakes and other disasters and crises.

title: Right to Health and strengthening community participation of the population, especially women, in Kwango. Democratic Republic of the Congo. Phase III
long_description: Health is an unguaranteed right in many countries such as the Democratic Republic of theCongo, where women, girls and vulnerable people in general suffer the serious effects ofhaving little or no access to basic health services. Contributing to reducing thissituation is the driving force behind this project, which is part of a broader strategywhose objective is to contribute to improving the right of access to health and improve the quality of lifeof the population of Kwango in the DRC.To address the problem, the project proposes two complementary lines of action: thefirst is the rehabilitation of the treatment room and the incorporation of equipment and materialsfor the general consultation and the laboratory of the Kindi Hospital, which, despite having thefacilities, the reference hospital in the area lacks adequate infrastructure. Thissituation causes an increase in the mortality rate and a deterioration in the health of the populationin Kwango. On the other hand, we want to continue working from a community and participation approach,fostering the empowerment of the local population, especially women, inhealth issues. title: Rural Infrastructure Support to PNPM Mandiri Project II
long_description: The Project forms part of the Government of Indonesia's ongoing flagship poverty reduction program the National Program for Community Empowerment (PNPM Mandiri). The Asian Development Bank (ADB) supports the PNPM Mandiri through the Rural Infrastructure Support to PNPM Mandiri Project I(RIS-PNPM I), which included community facilitation and mobilization, and rural infrastructure support in the four provinces of Jambi, Lampung, Riau, and South Sumatra. The Project continues the support for RIS-PNPM I, financing two cycles of village planning and block grants in about 1,500 villages in 215 kecamatans in four provinces. The Project follows a community-driven development approach and will empower communities, strengthen their capacity to prioritize, design, implement, and monitor community-based projects, and provide block grants to finance community-identified needs and priorities.

title: Réhabilitation du système de santé II
long_description: The Central African Republic is one of the poorest countries in the world. For decades, the landlocked country has suffered from numerous violent conflicts and weak state structures. This project addresses the particularly vulnerable health sector and builds on the content of the first phase 'Reconstruction of the Health System in CAR'. The aim of the project is to increase the use of qualitatively improved health services by the target group, especially women and children, in the project region. The rehabilitation and equipping of health facilities will be expanded to additional locations in the project area in Phase II. At the same time, support for the 16 facilities selected in Phase I will be continued in order to respond to continuing needs and to safeguard what has been achieved so far. Training capacity created in Phase I will be used in Phase II to address existing staffing and skills shortages at health care facilities. Complementary measures will be implemented to improve access to family planning information and products in the project area. The target group of the project is the population in the project regions, especially mothers, children and adolescents. The project area is Health Region 1, specifically the prefectures of Lobaye and Ombella M'Poko. The international and national Red Cross/Red Crescent are entrusted by the CAR government with the implementation of the measures.

Humanitarian interventions in fragile contexts, combined with poverty reduction and sustainable development are promoted through innovative work with children and youths.

Somerset III will invest in middle market growth companies that provide healthcare products and services to underserved segments of the population. Since inception, Somerset has been an advocate for developing and deepening access to affordable and quality healthcare in Tier II and Tier III cities in India.

title: Strengthening community-based health work for church health facilities in India

Measures include assistance in drawing up written agreements with health authorities and NGOs, counselling, treatment of malnutrition in children, community-based health services, health camps for the treatment/referral of patients by health workers and volunteers, dialogue at community level within the framework of self-help groups.

title: Strengthening Comprehensive Primary Health Care in Urban Areas Program under Pradhan Mantri Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana
long_description: The proposed results-based lending will support the government in improving equitable access to comprehensive primary health care in urban areas. The government prioritizes the comprehensive primary health care as a strategy to achieve continuum of health care and resilient health systems to the COVID-19 pandemic and future health emergencies. The program outcome will be achieved through (i) expanding the number and range of primary health care services, especially noncommunicable diseases, infectious disease surveillance, and specialist services, (ii) strengthening community outreach services for easier access to health care services as well as improved health seeking behaviors among the urban poor and the vulnerable, and (iii) strengthening urban health system capacity for comprehensive, quality primary health care. The program aims to increase the number of functional health and wellness centers to cater 256 million urban dwellers including 51 million urban slum dwellers in 13 states. The program is aligned with the government's Ayushman Bharat (Healthy India) as well as Pradhan Mantri Atmanirbhar Swasth Bharat Yojana (Epidemic / Disaster Preparedness and Response) programs.

title: Strengthening health facilities in Senegal

The project contributes to improving the population's access to quality health care. Measures include training for health workers, equipping them with medical equipment and providing them with information material.

title: Strengthening integral healthcare through health promoters in rural areas of Guatemala
long_description: The predominantly indigenous population in rural areas of Guatemala has historically been largely excluded from access to adequate healthcare. The aim is therefore to strengthen a local network of volunteer health promoters in the project region who offer integral health services. To this end, promoters will receive further training on medical, social and environmental issues and be supported by specialised staff. The target group are the promoters and the residents of rural communities.

title: Strengthening Primary Health Care in the Gaza Strip
long_description: The project aims to support the right to health and promote access to quality health services for the Palestinian population,the project aims to strengthen Primary Health Care in the Gaza Strip,as a priority level of care,the pivot of the entire system National Health. The project represents the advancement of previous initiatives,completing the computerization of services already started in the southern area also with funds from other donors and extending the same initiative to the central area,guaranteeing better and more efficient services to over half of the population in Gaza. The activities,participated by the Palestinian Ministry of Health,the World Health Organization,the local NGO PCRF and the Tuscan Global Health Center: IT equipment and installation of management database in 17 basic clinics and in 1 hospital, technical training of the related health and administrative operators, management training for executives.

title: Strengthening Resilience through Enhancing Health Service Facilities in Yemen - Phase V
long_description: In Yemen, approximately 18.2 million people - 55% of the population - were in need of humanitarian assistance in 2023. Access to basic healthcare services is not or only limitedly guaranteed for large parts of the population. The project aims to contribute to strengthening the resilience of healthcare facilities and the population in the project areas (Impact). This is intended to be achieved through the stabilization and improvement of access to and utilization of public healthcare facilities. Additionally, the project contributes to strengthening social cohesion with the aim of addressing the central needs of vulnerable population groups, particularly women, and increasing the utilization of healthcare services in the funded facilities across all population groups (Outcome). Key measures and results include: rehabilitation and refurbishment as well as equipping of healthcare facilities, including the stabilization of the functionality of water supply and sanitation, waste disposal, and electricity, training measures for healthcare personnel, and financing technical pilot studies. The target group of the project is the population of the selected districts with a special focus on vulnerable groups such as women. The project executing agency is the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS).

Adjuvant Global Health Technology Fund, L.P. seeks to invest in new or improved technologies for public health challenges that have been historically overlooked and that cause significant morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries. One of a small cohort of investments made to advance the Foundation's Catalytic Capital Consortium initiative, Adjuvant Global Health Technology Fund, L.P. uses catalytic capital to bridge access to innovative and transformative technology for difficult-to-reach people and places, helps build a meaningful track record for an expert team of global health and finance professionals, and signals the economic viability of investing with global health outcomes as the principal driver. The Foundation's impact investment will combine with catalytic capital from the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and others to help leverage a total combined investment pool of up to $300 million.

long_description: Denmark provides core and softly earmarked contribution to UNICEF under the Multilateral Partnership Agreement 2023-2025. Its mission is to advocate for the protection of children's rights, to help meet children's basic needs, and to expand opportunities for children to reach their full potential. title: WASH: Water Purification and Distribution of Hygiene Kits in Zaporizhzhia Oblast
long_description: The WASH: Water Purification and Distribution of Hygiene Kits in Zaporizhzhia Oblast project, implemented by ARCS Arci Culture Solidali in partnership with Fondazione Arca, aims to improve public health in the Zaporizhzhia region of Ukraine. This initiative responds to the deteriorating water supply conditions caused by the ongoing conflict. The project focuses on two main activities: Installation of water purification systems: The project will install modular water treatment systems with a capacity of at least 45 liters per hour at two key health facilities: the Regional Blood Service Center of Zaporizhzhia and the Regional Clinical Hospital for Infectious Diseases. This aims to ensure a constant flow of safe, potable water, enhancing the safety and effectiveness of medical treatments. The project also includes training hospital staff to operate and maintain these systems. Distribution of essential hygiene kits: The project will provide hygiene kits to 330 vulnerable families in the Zaporizhzhia Oblast. These kits contain essential personal and household hygiene items such as soap, toothbrushes, toothpaste, and other personal care products. The distribution also includes awareness materials in Ukrainian to promote good hygiene practices

The project will draw on available knowledge, develop and apply new models of family medicine in the clinics. It is a right based project that secures equal and fair opportunities of women, children and people with disabilities. The social and health education offered inside the clinics shall target gender equity, women's social and health rights, and meet gender specific needs.

title: Advisor for health infrastructure, capacity building and maintenance in a hospital in Bushulo, Ethiopia
long_description: The advisory assignment focuses on strengthening the capacity of the management team in developing a sustainable maintenance plan for hospital facilities and specialized medical equipment in Ethiopia. Conducted in cooperation with Caritas Vorarlberg, the assignment enhances technical maintenance competencies, ensuring compliance with required standards and fostering long-term operational sustainability. The advisor supports the technical maintenance team in improving their skills across various fields, enabling them to operate hospital systems independently while minimizing reliance on external assistance. The assignment fosters a professional working environment that is adaptable to technical emergencies and evolving medical technologies. A key focus is on enhancing communication skills within the maintenance team, particularly in technical interactions with both internal and external stakeholders. Key outcomes include the development of standard operating procedures (SOPs) for equipment related to electricity, medical gas, and biomedical machines to ensure long-term functionality. An annual maintenance task list is established, along with structured monitoring, documentation, and reporting systems for maintenance activities. Training workshops introduce methodologies for goal-oriented work and time tracking, improving efficiency and accountability. A significant milestone in the assignment is the successful relocation of the technical team to a designated department building. This shift optimizes workflow, strengthens team collaboration, and reduces communication barriers, enhancing overall hospital maintenance management. Through these efforts, the assignment contributes to the hospital's long-term infrastructure sustainability and improved healthcare service delivery.

Construction will begin in 2024 after studies and analyses conducted in 2022 and 2023 to identify the problem and define a project that can solve it. Meetings and seminars have already been held with the community and the authorities to share the purpose until reaching a unanimous consensus. The architectural project is a model of sustainability and will be implemented with the direct participation of the community, as is the case in all Balouo Salo projects. title: Consultant for WASH, infrastructure maintenance and waste management systems in Bushulo, Ethiopia
long_description: The advisory assignment focuses on improving water, sanitation, and waste management systems at a hospital in Hawassa, Ethiopia. Conducted in cooperation with Caritas Vorarlberg, the assignment provides technical guidance in developing and implementing sustainable water and waste management strategies while establishing a robust maintenance team. The assignment directly involves 25 individuals (5 female, 20 male) and indirectly benefits 2,100 people (2,000 female, 100 male). The advisor plays a key role in developing a comprehensive water maintenance concept for the hospital's five water cycles and distribution networks. Additionally, the assignment supports the creation of a state-of-the-art waste management strategy, including the development and implementation of a waste management handbook. A major aspect of the advisory work includes assisting in the installation of a waste incineration plant for infectious hospital waste and optimizing the purification processes of the existing biological sewage treatment plant. Other core responsibilities include advising on water supply management, wastewater treatment and disposal, solid waste management, composting, and rainwater usage. The advisor also supports the planning and implementation of alternative toilet solutions, such as separation toilets, composting toilets, and single-flush systems, to enhance sanitation infrastructure. Training and capacity-building for hospital staff ensure that the implemented strategies are sustainable and effectively managed in the long term. By combining structural modifications, staff training, and expert technical guidance, the assignment contributes to improving the hospital's overall sanitation, hygiene, and environmental sustainability, ensuring better health outcomes for patients and staff.

title: CZ Clinical Lab Improvement
long_description: As part of its efforts to improve health care, the National Pediatric Hospital in Phnom Penh focuses on the area of maternal and child care. This project is motivated by the need to respond to challenges in healthcare that are specific to the region and stem from the World Health Organization's recommendations for ISO 15189 standards. The main objective of the project is to improve the level and quality of health services, which will directly contribute to better health outcomes for mothers and their children. The project aims to systematically improve laboratory and diagnostic processes in line with international standards and best-practices. To do this, it uses modern methods and technologies with an emphasis on selection, validation and verification of laboratory testing procedures, and quality management of laboratory processes. Key outputs of the project include the introduction of standardised operating procedures, improvement of internal and external quality control systems, and strengthening the professional capacity of staff.The main implementer of the project is the National Paediatric Hospital in collaboration with the Vita et Futura Foundation, which already has experience with similar projects in this area. The common goal is to transfer the successful experiences and practices from the previous project and implement them in the newly developing programme, which is expected to contribute significantly to strengthening health care in Cambodia. The project strongly supports human rights and gender equality, reflecting OECD indicators number 8 and 9. By improving access to high-quality healthcare for mothers and newborns, the project contributes to strengthening healthcare as a fundamental human right. Specific measures to support health literacy and women's education also strengthen their social and economic equality. Additionally, involving women in decision-making processes and raising awareness about gender equality within the institution represents practical steps towards achieving gender equality.

title: F.a: Inclusive functional Education and Livelihoods Programme for Refugees
long_description: Ethiopia hosts over 820,000 refugees of which some 350,000 are South Sudanese and live in Gambella region and 71,000 majority being Eritrean, in urban Addis Ababa. The project targets these both groups contributing to enhanced resilience through education.The literacy rate among the South Sudanese is exceptionally low, only 27% (16% for female) and therefore the need for functional adult literacy (FAL) training in Gambella refugee camps is high. Basic functional literacy skills form a basis for personnal development and facilitate coping in everyday challenges. The literacy courses include basic information about health and nutrition as well as many other themes thus providing basic knowledge base to enable participants to improve their living conditions. Also English courses will be provided for those literate in their mother tongue. The FAL and English courses are also organised in the local communities close to the camps to enablee local residents equally benefit from the project. The gender relations are complex in the area both among the refugee and hosting communities. Women's socio-economic status is generally lower than men's. Improved literacy skills contribute positively to women's status. Taking this into consideration majority of planned 8000 participants to FAL and English courses will be women. Women's participation, and more particularly, breast-feeding mothers' inclusion will be encouraged by adjusting the course schedule to their convinient time, bring learning spaces close to their vicinity and hire child minders to look after the children during the courses. Disability inclusion is another core area of project and strategic partnerships have been established to ensure the required support for the identification of PWD, to provide assistive devices to PWD learners, and to establish a stronger referral network for PWDs. Although the urban refugee population have generally higher education levels than the South Sudanese refugees in Gambella, unemployment is high among the urban refugee population, leading to social challenges. Urban refugees, although allowed to work, have very limited opportunities to enter gainful and decent employment because of lacking the required skills or qualifications but also due to their status as refugees.To enhance refugees employability project provides vocational, entrepreneurial and life skills training to 800 urban refugees in cooperation with vocational institute(s).

title: Health System Strengthening - Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights III
long_description: The project (BMZ no. 2021 68 904) comprises the third phase of the programme 'Health System Strengthening - Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) in Togo', which has been implemented in the Kara region since May 2018 and will be extended to the Savanes and Centrale regions with the additional financing of Euro22 million. Togo remains one of the poorest countries in the world, with a per capita income of around USD 2 per day. Healthcare provision for the population in the area of sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) is precarious, particularly in rural areas. The maternal mortality rate was 36/100,000 in 2017 and the newborn mortality rate was 25/1,000 in 2020. The project addresses this problem. By strengthening the health system in the area of SRHR, a contribution is made to improving maternal and newborn health. The aim of the programme is to improve access, use and quality of health services and to increase demand. Under the programme, rural health facilities and district hospitals are to be rehabilitated, expanded and equipped with medical equipment (component 1). Targeted investment-related training and communication measures (components 2 and 3) support the improvement of quality and the creation of demand. The family planning services in the communities are also supported and expanded. The project executing agency is the Togolese Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé, de l'Hygiène Publique et de l'Accès Universel aux Soins), which delegates implementation to the regional directorate. The target group of Phase III of the programme continues to be the rural and predominantly poor population, particularly women of childbearing age and newborns in the Centrale and Savanes regions.

title: In collaboration with 'Reach for a Dream': converting a bathroom in St. Joseph's Intermediate Pediatric Care facility into a new therapy room.
long_description: For many children and young people with complex medical and rehabilitative needs, there is an inadequate range of intermediate care in the Western Cape. Many patients fall through the cracks because they are either not healthy enough to go home or not sick enough to stay in an acute care hospital. Active since 1935, the 175-bed St. Joseph's Intermediate Pediatric Care facility in Montana provides multidisciplinary care for children ages 0-18 with life-limiting or life-threatening illnesses such as cerebral palsy, infectious diseases, traumatic brain injury, neurology and oncology provides temporary health care for medically fragile children. In collaboration with the 'Reach for a Dream' Foundation, an existing bathroom in St. Joseph's Intermediate Pediatric Care facility will be converted into a new therapy room - a so-called 'Dream Room'. In 2018, the foundation launched the 'Dream Rooms concept' - rooms in hospitals or children's wards and facilities are converted to be child-friendly. The aim is to create creative, safe and friendly and inviting spaces for children in which the children feel comfortable and can ignore their illness and the hospital atmosphere for a certain time. The organization needs funding to renovate a bathroom into a new children's therapy room. Over a period of one month, the organization wants to dismantle the existing bathroom furnishings including all pipes and connections, paint the walls, repair the floors, and install the new 'dream room' furnishings.
