title: NCD Alliance 2020-2024 - ISK NCD Alliance 2020-2022
long_description: The intervention concerns core support to NCD Alliance (NCDA) for operations covering the period August 2020 – December 2024. The amount for the contribution is 21,600,000 SEK.NCD Alliance (NCDA) is a unique global civil society network that unites international, regional and national civil society organisations, alliances and networks dedicated to improving non-communicable disease (NCD) prevention and control worldwide. Through its member alliances, it has developed a network of over 2,000 civil society organisations in 170 countries working towards the NCD agenda. NCDA is considered a global thought leader, and a civil society voice, on NCD policy and practice. It works to elevate the NCDs onto the global health and development agenda and also to bridge the gap and translate global commitments to the ground at the national level. It does this through its own organisation as well as its members by leading and coordinating advocacy towards political processes at all levels and promoting accountability and knowledge exchange. It also leads a variety of initiatives and in-depth programmes to develop civil society capacity in low- and middle income countries (LMICs) to deliver progress on NCD prevention and control at the international, regional and national levels. NCDA is seated in Geneva, Switzerland. It consists of 108 member alliances, networks and organisations representing a wide range of diseases, risk factors and thematic priorities across the NCD spectrum (including mental illness and air pollution). NCDA has four founding members, each representing one of the main four types of NCDs. The founding members are: The International Union against Tuberculosis and Lung Disease (The Union), the Union for International Cancer Control (UICC), the World Heart Federation (WHF) and the International Diabetes Federation (IDF). NCDA has requested organisational support from Sida to operationalise its strategy over the next three years. NCDA will utilize Sida support to expand its advocacy and prevention work, expand its capacity development programmes and strengthen its organisational development and effectiveness. NCDA has submitted its Strategic Plan (SP), Budget and Results Framework for 2016 – 2020. NCDA is currently developing its new strategic plan for 2021- 2028 and have conveyed that it does not expect significant strategic changes.

title: Role of PIEZO1 in mediating phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure on red blood cells (RBCs) in patients with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)
long_description: Programme: Wellcome Accelerator Awards. Description: This project aims to elucidate the role of the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 in regulating phosphatidylserine (PS) exposure on red blood cells (RBCs) among patients with Sickle Cell Disease (SCD). SCD, a genetic disorder, results in RBC deformation that precipitates severe vaso-occlusive crises and subsequent organ damage. By employing high-throughput electrophysiology via the Automated Patch Clamp (APC) system alongside physiological flow simulations using the ibidi pump system, the study aims to quantify PIEZO1 activity in sickle RBCs. Research efforts will extend to examining mechanotransduction changes under variable solution application speeds and oxygen deprivation. Further investigations will assess the influence of cytoskeletal modifications on PIEZO1 function. Finally, a pivotal aspect of the study involves correlating PIEZO1 activity with RBC phenotypic traits, such as PS exposure and cellular adhesion to endothelial linings. Through this comprehensive methodology, the project intends to uncover the pivotal contributions of PIEZO1 to SCD pathophysiology and to identify potential therapeutic targets that could alleviate disease manifestations. Integrating cutting-edge electrophysiological techniques with precise simulations of physiological conditions, the research is poised to offer profound insights into the biophysical characteristics of PIEZO1 and its consequential effects on RBC dynamics in SCD.

title: Campus sexual harassment: exploring its causes, interventions and breaking the silence of victims
long_description: Background: Sexual harassment on campuses of the Nigerian universities is a major problem affecting students. It inflicts long-lasting effects on the psychological and emotional well-being of students especially when they fail to disclose information about their ordeal. This culture of silence undermines any meaningful or sustainable remediation of sexual harassment.Objective: To investigate the multifaceted, immediate and remote causes of campus sexual harassment, elucidating the factors that contribute to its prevalence and develop interventions and policies to empower victims, aiding them to willingly volunteer information to break the silence, mitigate sexual harassment and create a safer and more inclusive campus environment. Methodology: The study adopts a mixed method research design: the integration of qualitative and quantitative methods. A structured survey questionnaire and a semi-structured face-to-face interview are the primary methods of data collection. The population comprises the students of the universities in the South-South geopolitical zone of Nigeria. The sample consists of 400 male and female students of 6 private universities in the 6 states of the South-South geopolitical zone. Mixed methods, content analysis, descriptive and regression, would be employed in analysing the data collected from the sampled participants. Findings: The findings will inform evidence-based interventions including policies and programmes, for the creation of a safer educational environment, providing a solid empirical foundation for transformative change in addressing campus sexual harassment. The research will fill up a research gap that would positively impact universities and society generally.

title: F.a: Enhancing Well-being of Migrant Workers
long_description: Migration for foreign employment has become a major source of income for the Nepalese. Though this has brought economic profits to many Nepali households and the nation, it has come with a costs. Those are the psychological stress and mental health problems, resulting in family disintegration,emotional and behavioral problems of children. Studies on living and working conditions of low-skilled migrants consistently revealed abuse and exploitation, including forced labor and trafficking. These ar reflected also on the migrants' family members during the absence but above all during the home living periods of the migrant workers. The trauma experinced by the returning migrant workers, or their families, are not spoken of, resulting in behavioral problems, reduced efficiency, loosing comprehension and cognitive ability, withdrawal etc. These have a ngatve impact on person's human relationships, wellbeing, health and and productivity. As a result of project, migrant workers and their families have improved their mental health and psychosocial wellbeing. Returnee migrant worker and their families have been engaged in self-employment, business or other livelihood initiatives. Also, local government has replicated the best practices of the project with sustained allocation or resources. The project beneficiaries are the 2 560 migrant workers and their families, and 1 200 government officials and members of the organizations of persons with disabilities (DPOs) in Kailali and Salyan districts. The project is implemented by Centre for Mental Health and Counseling Nepal (CMC-Nepal) (https://www.cmcnepal.org.np/).

title: F.a: From Survivors to Agents of Change
long_description: The peace agreement between the Colombian government and the FARC did not bring peace to the country. Violence against human rights defenders and community leaders has escalated, and armed groups are fighting for control of areas ceded by the FARC. Around 12 000 Colombians have been killed or injured in landmine accidents since 1990, of whom about 40% are civilians. More landmines are being planted all the time. People injured in accidents face difficulties in asserting their rights due to lack of information, poor access to services, and attitudinal and legal barriers. Application processes are long and complex, and practical obstacles include long distances, poor internet access and the attitudes of officials. The programme of psychosocial support for people injured in landmine accidents is not available in rural areas. The project aims to improved quality of life of landmine survivors, and their ability to defend the rights through their own organisations, also participating in activities to prevent further accidents. Immediate results: i) in the provinces of Arauca, Chocó and Guaviare, people injured in landmine accidents receive psychosocial support, legal assistance and peer support, ii) members of indigenous and Afro-Colombian communities have learned and are applying safe practices to avoid further accidents, and iii) Self-help organisations of people injured in mine accidents have strengthened and increased their advocacy and independently provide mine accident prevention training and support, with the permission of the national authority.Beneficiaries are persons injured in landmine accidents in Arauca, Chocó and Guaviare, their own organizations and communities. The implementing partner is Lutheran World Federation (LWF), an international actor with presence in its areas of operation and working with local communities and organisations. Its strength is a holistic approach, the triple nexus of humanitarian, development and peace work. The gained trust and credibility among other civil society actors, authorities and armed actors allows access to conflict areas, facilitates establishing links between communities and local authorities, contributing to the improvement of living conditions for communities and paving the way for advocacy at regional, national and international level. https://www.lutheranworld.org/

title: F.a: Innovative Education and Peaceful Living Environment for Children and Youth in Iraq
long_description: The situation in Iraq is fragile after the cycle of conflict, war and ISIS rule. Nearly half of the population live in poverty. Children's right to education is unfulfilled in most parts of the country due to poor access to education and a severe lack of resources.Conditions are especially dire in Kurdistan, where children and youth have long lived in the midst of conflict and instability. Fida's Country Programme aims to ensure quality education and a safe living environment for children and youth in Iraq. The goal is to reduce dropout rates and bullying in schools, and to raise awareness on the rights of children with disabilities.Fida partners with several local organisations, including Together to Protect Human and Environment Association, Halabja Disabled Organisation, Yes We Can – Network of local NGOS, and Assemblies of God Kurdistan. Work is implemented in four locations: Erbil, Halabja, Ninewa and Kirkuk.Teachers are trained on inclusive education and child-led teaching methods. The sustainable school model, as well as the accompanying teacher's guide are expanded to new schools. Access to education for children with disabilities is promoted through awareness raising campaigns. Children learn about their rights in clubs and camps. Communities receive training and seminars for psychosocial support.Fida, in cooperation with partner organisation Together, universities and private companies, pilots an entrepreneurship training and mentoring programme. Its aim is to provide opportunities for young people in vulnerable situations, such as refugees, to start new businesses and contribute to building a more innovation-friendly society.

title: F.a: School Mental Health Program
long_description: Mental health problems are still not adequately identified, prevented, and treated in Nepal. Especially school-going children of ultra-poor families and children with disabilities are at risk of developing mental health and psychosocial problems. The recent study (2020) carried out by the Nepal Health Research Council has revealed that the mental health problems are found among 5.2% children of the age group from 13 to 17 years, whereas these problems increased to 10% above 18 years. Due to lack of awareness about emotional and behavioral problems (EBPs) of children, teachers and parents practice corporal punishment. Student counselling is not avalable at school. There is a serious problem in student drop out and EBPs. The impact of the project is that the school-going children and adolescent are able to develop to their full potential, and their learning result improve as their psychosocial wellbeing grows stronger.Teachers have increased capacity to practice child friendly classroom management and parenting education.Parent and other stakeholders have increased their support in promotion of psychosocial wellbeing of children. Child protection policy and practice are in place in project schools. School based psycho-social support unit is functioning in program schools. Selfhelp Groups protect the rights of the persons with mental health and psycho-social disabilities. By 2025, master trainers are developed at national, province and local level to replicate comprehensive school counseling. CMC-Nepal has increased collaboration with the Government of Nepal to formulate and endorse comprehensive school counselling policy.The project beneficiaries are school going children and adolescents, with especial focus on children with emotional and behavioral problems, other students in the project area, adults with mental health and psychosocial problems, and parents, families, and care takers of these people. The project is implemented by Centre for Mental Health and Counseling Nepal (CMC-Nepal) (https://www.cmcnepal.org.np/).

title: F.a: Strengthening Psychosocial Disability Rights
long_description: Persons with psychosocial disability face daily barriers due to inhumane treatment, discrimination and exclusion in society which is further exacerbated by lack of strong disability rights and protection laws in Nepal. There is a need to identify persons with psychosocial disability and support them in their recovery, build a strong network among them as well as empower them about their rights, form a coalition with underrepresented disability groups and encourage them to demand for their rights with the duty bearers at their local and province level. Moreover, there is a need to sensitize families and communities regarding psychosocial disability and support in their social inclusion and improving livelihood. This project aims to respond to these needs and the results of project activities are: MPs from the Federal and Province Parliament take measures to formulate psychosocial disability friendly laws or amend laws which are discriminatory / derogatory towards persons with psychosocial disability, bureaucrats from the federal, province and local level take measures to include psychosocial disability in the plans and programs which are developed, and persons with psychosocial disabilities and coalition of underrepresented groups are engaged in evidence based self-advocacy to mainstream psychosocial disability in Sudurpaschhim Province and Karnali Province. The project beneficiaries are 670 persons with disabilities (including psychosocial disability) and their family members, members of National Federation of Disabled Nepal (NFDN), members of community groups (womens groups, youth groups, agriculture groups, religious groups, consumer groups) and journalists, and 230 government officlas and law-makers in the local, provincial and federal level. The project is implemented by Koshish - National Mental Health Self-Help Organization (https://www.koshishnepal.org/).

title: F.a: Supporting socio-economic re/integration and ensuring equal participation rights for repatriated and refugee women and girls in Kosovo
long_description: 1) Kosovo has a long history of migration. Citizens of Kosovo have migrated not only before or during the war, but also more recently, seeking to improve their livelihood and opportunities. Some of the citizens have returned, whether forcibly or willingly, and others are yet to be repatriated, especially, but not only, from European countries. Furthermore, in the last decade, there has been an increased number of persons with international protection status seeking protection and refugee status in Kosovo. The state institutions in Kosovo are facing multiple challenges and issues in their efforts to successfully integrate and reintegrate the Repatriated Persons and Refugees, in particular Repatriated Women and Girls and Women and Girls with International Protection Status (RWG and WGIPS). These include insufficient capacities, in particular of the municipal level bodies dealing directly with the RWG and WGIPSs and their families. In addition, the multiple vulnerabilities of RWG and WGIPS prevent them from accessing psychosocial and economic empowerment services to increase their socio-economic well-being and from active engagement in society.2) This project contributes to the socio-economic re/integration and to ensuring equal participation rights for repatriated and refugee women and girls in Kosovo. This will be done through providing direct psychosocial support and economic empowerment services to the RWGs and WGIPs, as well as through strengthening the capacities of municipal and state institutions to provide psychosocial and reintegration services to these beneficiaries. 3) Repatriated women and girls and Women and girls with international protection status (refugees) in the Republic of Kosovo through direct psychosocial support and economic empowerment – up to 50 beneficiaries per year. Institution officials at municipal and central levels and professionals offering services to the RWG and WGIPSs – up to 240 professionals and officials in 4 years. 4) Implementing partners: Kosova Centre for Rehabilitation of Torture Victims (KRCT) https://krct.org/ , Jesuite Refugee Service (JRS) https://jrs.net/en/country/kosovo/The project is implemented in cooperation with the Kosovo Ministry of Internal Affairs

title: F.a: Trust and Peace in Communities - Horn of Africa
long_description: 1) The Horn Africa Region has experienced violent conflicts that have led to traumatic experiences among its people, including civil wars, interethnic cross-border conflicts, inter-communal conflicts. Approximately 50% of current peace processes fail during their first three to four years. Few of them have undertaken to uncover the massive trauma of affected communities and to build trust and peace at the grassroot level, failing to end the cycle of violence. This proportion of failure presents an urgent need to identify additional methods incorporating durable and sustainable transformation and reconciliation within communities experiencing conflict. In order to improve the efficacy of peace and reconciliation processes, engaging and supporting insider reconcilers' (local reconciliation practitioners) leadership is critical. This project seeks to support reconciliation practitioners' leadership, wellbeing, and reach as these individuals transform conflicts within the Horn of Africa. 2) The project contributes to increased resiliency to conflict of affected communities through supporting and sustaining 200 local insider reconcilers from the Horn of Africa by the end of 2025.This will be achieved through strengthening the role and capacity of Insiders Reconcilers to stabilize conflicts. This will be done through equipping them with knowledge and skills of peace processes, fostering the integration of skills on trauma and psychosocial support to reconciliation work, and supporting reconciliation process design and mechanisms development, with a focus on peer learning.3) 200 insider reconcilers (community leaders, faith leaders, women leaders, youth leaders, leaders of minorities and people representing specific institutions) from the Horn of Africa region.4) Implementing partners: Mary Hoch Foundation (https://www.thinkpeacehub.org/), Maandeeq Mental Health (https://maandeeqmh.org/about/)

title: F.a: Trust and Peace: Peace Building from the Ground
long_description: 1) From 1955 to present, South Sudan has been in a near-constant state of civil war with Sudan and internally with periodic ceasefires. Nine years after independence, the country is one of the world's most fragile, insecure and vulnerable countries. The high failure of current peace processes presents an urgent need to identify additional methods incorporating durable and sustainable transformation and reconciliation within communities experiencing conflict. Religious leaders and other peace actors are constantly called upon to act as local reconcilers in old and new conflicts without adequate skills, support and mentorship in critical areas. They are also needed to offer psychosocial support to suffering communities whilst themselves are subject to psychosocial stresses without the skills and support necessary. Women and youth are even less likely to have the necessary skills and support to perform their roles and act as peace builders within their communities, jeopardizing the sustainability of peace efforts at the grassroots level. The challenges in peacebuilding at the grassroots make efforts at the national level more difficult, as the necessary trust lacks at the community level to support cohesion and nation building.2) The project contributes to peaceful and reconciled communities through enhanced ability of religious leaders to act as communities' insider reconcilers and healers in the project target regions by the end of 2025. This will be achieved through strengthening the role and capacity of Insiders Reconcilers to stabilize conflicts in South Sudan. Insider Reconcilers will be equipped with knowledge and skills of peace processes, including skills on trauma and psychosocial support, and supported in reconciliation process design and mechanisms development, with a focus on peer learning.3) 200 (95M, 95F, 10 PwDs) religious actors including women of faith and interfaith youth, and local community peace actors, in the 3 historical states of South Sudan (the Bahr el ghazal state, the Great Upper Nile and the Equatoria states)4) Implementing partner: African Council of Religious Leaders- Religions for Peace (ACRL-RfP)https://www.acrl-rfp.org/

title: Gaza Community Mental Health Programme-Strategic Plan support 2022-2024 - Gaza Community Mental Health Programme strategic plan support 2022-2024
long_description: Support GCMHP in Gaza to provide specialized and holistic mental health services to vulnerable population and promote mental. health rights. GCMHP was established in 1990 as a non-government organization (NGO) in Palestine to introduce community mental healthcare to Gaza and provide specialized mental health and psychosocial services guided by the principles of justice and human rights. GCMHP aims to improve the mental health sector in the Gaza Strip through awareness raising, education, capacity building, scientific research, advocacy, lobbying, mobilization, treatment, and rehabilitation activities.GCMHP focuses on offering specialized community mental health services and is considered a resource in the mental health field for other community-based organizations (CBOs) in Gaza, the Ministry of Health, and UNRWA. GCMHP's mission is: 'Guided by the principles of justice and human rights, Gaza Community Mental Health Programme provides gender sensitive, inclusive, integrated, and specialized community mentalhealth services in Palestine'.Sweden has supported GCMHP's previous strategic period of 2019-2021 along with the Norwegian Representative Office and the Swiss Development Cooperation. The focus of the 2019-2021 strategic period was on improving the mental health of the population in the Gaza Strip through providing access to specialized mental health services.The focus for GCMHP in the upcoming strategic period 2022-2024 is on designing programs and interventions that promote and facilitate the access of the most vulnerable groups to mental health services, especially youth and people with disabilities (PwDs). This is in addition to upgrading and digitalization of a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning-MEAL system, and conducting relevant trainings for staff. Seeking partnerships with international and regional academic institutions and specialized centers and introducing a new (self-help) approach reaching larger population. GCMHP will focus on enhancing the use of modern technology in implementation of the Programme's long distance and face-to-face activities as well as enhancing action and updating policies related to feedback and complaints policy including protection of sexual abuse and exploitation issues (PSEA).The type of support to GCMHP from Sweden is core support. The intervention entails Sweden's contribution to GCMHP's core budget to work towards the following three strategic goals: 1. contribute to improving the mental health situation of the population in the Gaza Strip, 2. contribute to developing the mental health and psychosocial sector in the Gaza Strip, and 3. contribute to anchoring human rights-based principles and practices, reducing violence and promoting community resilience. Throughout the years, GCMHP strengthened its role as a leading organization in the fields of mental health and human rights through the provision of gender-sensitive, inclusive, evidence-based quality services, and being sensitive and responsive to the needs. Those needs were increasing as he living conditions in Gaza deteriorated over decades of occupation and continuous violations of human rights. In May and June 2021 several needs assessment reports stressed the need for special mental health services focusing on vulnerable groups specifically children and women. These assessments were prepared just after the 4th large scale offensive on Gaza (within 13 years) came to an end. Those reports, the evaluation recommendations, and internationally recommended practices helped shape GCMHP's 6th Strategic Plan.

title: Gaza Mental Health Program
long_description: The main goal of this project is to support mental health services in Gaza Strip to improve the well-being of the Palestinians living in Gaza. This support is a joint effort with Sweden and SDC, considering the level of hardship and stress in the Gaza Strip. The grant is intended to maintain and strengthen the mental health services provided to socially and emotionally stressed Palestinians, especially women and children affected by the conflict. The recipient advocates for women and children to access adequate mental health services through the grant. The recipient will prioritize mentally ill and disabled Palestinians by providing mental health assessment, counselling and treatment. The recipient conducts extensive assessments and research to study trends, needs, underlying causes and the effectiveness of assessment and treatment protocols. It is relevant to SDG 5 as the grant contributes to preventing discrimination and household violence and ending harmful practices and supports women to be more active in their societies and ensure access to essential mental health services.

title: HelpAge 2020-2024 - ISK HelpAge 2020-2024
long_description: Established in 1983, HelpAge International (HAI) is a civil society organisation that supports older people to claim their rights and challenge discrimination and poverty, so that they can lead dignified, secure, active and healthy lives. The organization represents a global network of civil society organisations working to promote and protect the rights of older women and men in nearly 90 countries, with over 157 member organisations, the majority of which are located in Low and Middle Income Countries (LMICs). HAI works with a wide range of activities, covering advocacy, development and humanitarian operations.In the previous collaboration (2015-2019), core funding from Sida supported a 5 year strategy (2015-2020) with a focus on income, health and care, voice and inclusion (gender and disability). During this period, HAI has specifically strengthened their work with health systems strengthening (also in collaboration with WHO), Non Communicable Diseases (NCDs), including mental health, and mainstreaming gender equality and inclusion (focus on disability). This contribution refers to core funding support from Sida to enable HAI to implement their new 10 year strategy (2020-2030). The 2030 strategy identifies 10 focus areas (including health and education) to achieve a positive impact on the quality of life of the poorest older people, with a focus on wellbeing, dignity and voice. Of the 10 focus areas, the 2020-22 planning priorities include: 1. Inspire a movement for change, 2. Promote age-inclusive systems, 3. Champion healthy ageing, 4. Deliver inclusive humanitarian action, 5. Challenge violence, abuse and neglect. Complementary to the Core Activities, additional support targets HAI's Global COVID-19 Response Plan. An amendment of agreement for nexus-support to the Ukraine crises was decided in March 2022.

title: Helping the helpers: supporting civil society organisations (CSOs) to protect persons with disabilities and victims of domestic violence in Tajikistan
long_description: The aim is to strengthen the resilience of grassroots civil society organizations that work to protect people with disabilities and victims of domestic violence in Tajikistan After an open call for proposals and careful selection by an independent evaluation committee, 80-100 activists from grassroots civil society organizations working to protect people with disabilities and victims of domestic violence will receive mini-scholarships that will give them access to relief measures, psychological support and, in rare exceptional cases medical help.

title: Hemayah: Protecting and Empowering Marginalized Communities
long_description: Egypt is a destination country for migrants and forcibly displaced persons facing challenging humanitarian conditions and limited prospects for integration. Switzerland will contribute to the Hemayah/Protection project implemented by Terre des Hommes to improve survival, protection, self-reliance, and wellbeing of migrants and forcibly displaced persons from marginalized communities. The project will provide comprehensive services and opportunities for skills development and socioeconomic integration through a sustainable community based approach.

title: Humanit. response, dissemination of life-saving messages, provision of assistance to victims of explosive remnants of war for affected Palestinians
long_description: The protection of Palestinians affected by the conflict in Gaza through a robust humanitarian response and preparedness, the dissemination of life-saving messages, and the provision of assistance to victims of explosive ordnance is ensured. 1: An emergency Explosive Ordnance Disposal intervention embedded within the overall humanitarian response in Gaza is in place 2: Conflict-affected communities have increased knowledge regarding protection risks, through Explosive Ordnance Risk Education and Conflict Preparedness and Protection : 3: EO victims have access to physical and functional rehabilitation including prosthetics and orthotics as well as Mental Health and Psychosocial support services

title: Humour gives hope: Strengthening the mental health of vulnerable children & young people in Palestine through health clowning
long_description: The project provides holistic and cost-effective mental and psychosocial support through artistic and humorous approaches, especially through health clowning, in health as well as social and crisis situations, to sustainably strengthen the mental health & resilience of vulnerable traumatised children and children with disabilities. Direct psychosocial and mental health support for vulnerable children. Capacity building on the use of art and humour for health for caregivers & social workers and artists. Improved awareness raising & networking to mainstream the health clowning approach in Palestine.

title: ICRC in the RCRC Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Movement Hub and Roadmap: Implementing the adopted MHPSS policy & resolution
long_description: This contribution enables ICRC to fully engage in transforming the IFRC Psychosocial Centre to a Movement wide MHPSS Hub with a shared and sustainable governance model. The Hub will bolster the impact of the Movement in providing access to MHPSS in varying types of crises worldwide, and strengthen Movement wide cooperation, complementarity and division of labor in general. This is a specific contribution in addition to the Netherlands unearmarked support to the Movement, which is provided on the understanding that the development and operationalization of the Hub requires enhanced efforts and involvement for which the ICRC and the Movement risk to lack resources, given the current accumulation of crises. This temporary addition ensures that ICRC expertise, linked to its mandate, will be well embedded in the set-up of the Hub. Moreover, it supports implementing the MHPSS Roadmap until the 34th RCRC Conference, and consultations and work of the Hub in the year thereafter.

title: Implementation of a partnership initiative in northern Iraq to promote humanitarian projects and the development of thematic clusters.
long_description: The main aim of the project is to strengthen the foundations of the partnership between Baden-Württemberg and Dohuk and to secure this cooperation in the long term.

title: Improved mental health and psychosocial support for Syrian refugees and vulnerable people in Lebanon
long_description: Improving access to mental health support services among young people,particularly coming from vulnerable Lebanese and conflictaffected Syrian refugee families,by providing essentials MHPSS services in 4 sites and by establishing tailored Peer Support Groups.

title: Improved WASH Facilities as well as Child and Youth Protection for Rohingya Camps and Host Communities
long_description: Nearly 1 million Rohingya refugees from Myanmar live in 33 overcrowded camps in Cox's Bazar, one of Bangladesh's already poorest districts and most vulnerable to natural disasters. Both their access to quality WASH services and child and adolescent protection remain poor. The project promotes the overall health, well-being, resilience, and protection from violence and neglect of Rohingya refugees in the camps and vulnerable people in the adjacent host communities. Project objectives include, first, providing the target group with equitable, inclusive, and hygienic access to water and sanitation (Component 1: WASH). Second, to better protect children and youth from all forms of violence, exploitation and neglect through equitable and inclusive access to quality child protection services, while benefiting from a strengthened environment (Component 2: Child and Youth Protection). A key objective of this project with significant influence on project design is to promote gender equality. Key interventions to achieve the objective include the construction, upgrading and maintenance of additional water supply networks, latrines and fecal sludge treatment facilities, procurement and distribution of menstrual hygiene kits (Component 1), construction of 11 additional and expansion of 15 existing multipurpose centers, individual case management for 6,000 young victims of violence, training of youth 'social change agents' within the community, and community sensitization and mobilization on combating harmful and discriminatory social norms and practices (Component 2). The project is being implemented by UNICEF in Cox's Bazar district. The target group is Rohingya who have fled Myanmar and residents of host communities.

title: Improvement of community-based social offers for refugees and vulnerable residents of host communities in Turkey
long_description: In Turkey, more than three million refugees live, the majority of whom are from Syria. Despite significant efforts, the country faces the challenge of providing these refugees and disadvantaged individuals from host communities with access to social services. The devastating earthquakes in 2023 and the strained economic situation have further exacerbated the situation. Particularly affected are disadvantaged groups such as single mothers, children, and people with disabilities. The political upheaval in Syria in 2024 has further impacted the situation of Syrian refugees. However, a large portion of Syrian refugees will remain in Turkey for several more years and will continue to rely on support. The aim of the project is to improve the personal, social, and economic resilience of refugees and disadvantaged groups in Turkish host communities. To achieve this, a civil society network called Akran Destek A?? (ADA Türkiye) will be established to improve access to social services. Experienced Turkish organizations will support smaller, local initiatives in hard-to-reach communities within this network to ensure the availability and quality of social services. This mentoring will be complemented by professional training. By combining humanitarian aid with the structural anchoring of social services, the project implements the Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDP-Nexus) approach. The project's areas of action include improving protection and access to social services, enhancing extracurricular education offerings, promoting social cohesion, and strengthening structures for social services and crisis management.

title: Improvement of the quality of life of children and young people with intellectual disabilities in four impoverished areas in Eastern Harare
long_description: This project aims to improve the quality of life of children and young people with intellectual disabilities and their families living in four impoverished communities in the eastern part of Harare. The quality of life of these people is poor for several reasons: - Limited number of service providers for people with intellectual disabilities and few interventions. - Limited access to occupational and physiotherapy for people over the age of two. - Families cannot afford the cost of regular therapy for their children. - Traditional cultural beliefs often lead to stigmatization and exclusion of children and their mothers The project envisages four main measures: - Free access to ergo and physiotherapy treatment for 300 children and young people with intellectual disabilities in four suburbs in the east of Harare will be provided. - Therapeutic techniques and knowledge will be imparted to 300 primary caregivers. They are empowered to pass on the techniques to at least two other family members and are engaged in building a community of peers. - Gatekeepers are continuously involved in the project and receive targeted training through two specific workshops. - Capacity is built through the in-depth engagement and training of potential new employees and through ongoing training and development programs for current employees.

title: Improving living conditions in shelters and centers and providing humanitarian and psychological first aid to internally displaced persons
long_description: The project is aimed at improving living conditions in shelters in the Dnepropetrovsk region, where material and psychosocial first aid will be provided to the most vulnerable members of the communities - primarily internally displaced persons (IDPs) and, thanks to the mobile team, also to other people most affected by the war. The project will consist of three main activities:1. Equipping 6 shelters and centers for IDPs according to their needs (first 3.5 months of the project).Thanks to the implementation of this part of the project, the living conditions of at least 1,000 internally displaced persons (including rotation) will be improved. 2. Social support of 1,600 households through the distribution of 10,150 vouchers for the purchase of food, medicines and drugstores (the next 8.5 months of the project). 3. Psychological first aid for alleviating and processing traumas caused by the ongoing military conflict in the country for adults and children in the form of group (direct beneficiaries of aid 1780 people + 3420 indirect beneficiaries) and individual sessions (direct beneficiaries of aid 330 people + 470 indirect beneficiaries).The aid will be provided on the basis of coordination with the UN clusters, which help to coordinate aid to the victims of the ongoing conflict within the region.

title: Improving the well-being of vulnerable children and families in remote areas in Albania

Homework supervision and psychosocial support for 25 children, provision of therapies for 7 children with increased support needs, summer camps for 60 children, support and strengthening of 3 child protection centers by training five employees and providing 100 therapeutic treatments, distribution of food and hygiene packages, further training in the integrative, educational field for 20 teachers and psychological support and encouragement for 300 young people

title: Increased access to education opportunities and strengthened child protection services, Ph. II
long_description: Türkiye currently has 85 million people (almost 30% of whom are children and young people). The country is also home to the world's largest recorded refugee population, with around 4 million refugees. At the end of 2023, around 3.2 million Syrians are under 'temporary protection' in Türkiye, as well as about 300,000 asylum seekers from Afghanistan, Iraq, Iran, Somalia and Ukraine as well as Palestine. More than 400,000 refugee children in Türkiye lack access to education and are acutely exposed to numerous risks of protection, including isolation, discrimination, economic exploitation and various forms of violence. The project therefore aims to improve the opportunities for refugee children and vulnerable children and young people in Türkiye to exercise their rights to protection and education. This will be achieved through a range of measures that increase access to education, early childhood education and protection services, such as prevention of gender-based violence and psychosocial support, for children, adolescents and their families at risk. The project is aimed at the target group of the most vulnerable children and young people, including their families, in Türkiye. These are mainly refugee children, including vulnerable Turkish children. The project, with a budget of EUR 14.5 million, will be implemented by UNICEF in 12 regions of Türkiye.

title: L'amélioration des conditions de vie en RDC
long_description: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has faced decades of violence, leading to a severe humanitarian crisis with nearly 7 million internally displaced persons (IDPs). The ongoing conflict, driven by armed groups, resource competition, and poor governance, has resulted in significant human rights abuses and economic decline. The psychological impact of this violence is profound, with high rates of mental health issues among the population, yet access to mental health services is severely limited. The World Health Organization estimates that a significant portion of the population suffers from anxiety, depression, and post-traumatic stress disorder, with only a fraction receiving adequate care. The project aims to address these challenges by integrating mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) into social cohesion programming in Tanganyika Province. It focuses on five key areas: reducing stigma around mental health, improving access to MHPSS services, enhancing the capacity of health facilities, developing standardized procedures for mental health care, and fostering social cohesion to break cycles of violence. The overall objective is to increase community resilience to conflict by providing culturally appropriate, gender-sensitive, and economically accessible MHPSS services. The project will directly benefit over 157,000 individuals through community-based MHPSS services, training for local health staff, and the establishment of social cohesion centers. It will also engage local communities in participatory activities to ensure ownership and sustainability. By addressing the psychosocial needs of both men and women, the project aims to promote gender equality and empower communities to actively participate in peacebuilding efforts. The integration of MHPSS into broader social initiatives is expected to enhance community resilience, foster social trust, and ultimately contribute to sustainable peace in the region.

title: Medical aid and promoting resilience: partnership support between Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg and Kyiv-Darnytsia
long_description: The ongoing military aggression against Ukraine has plunged the country into a humanitarian emergency. The consequences of the war, which are being felt far beyond Ukraine, will continue to affect Europe for many years to come. It is therefore urgently necessary to create sustainable structures to ensure both humanitarian aid on the ground and support for refugees in host countries such as Germany. In this context, we have developed a two-pronged project that combines direct aid in Darnytsya, a district of Kyiv, with support measures in Berlin. The aim is to strengthen German-Ukrainian cooperation and create long-term prospects for overcoming the consequences of the war. This project is made up of two central components. Component 1: Medical care in Darnytsya The medical infrastructure in Ukraine has been severely affected by the war. There is a lack of basic medical equipment and materials in Darnytsya. This is where the first project component comes in: With the support of Aid Pioneers and funding from the district fund, a container of medical supplies worth around half a million euros is being sent to Darnytsya. Aid Pioneers is in close contact with the local hospitals and is coordinating the list of requirements with the delivery options. Logistics and implementation are also organised by Aid Pioneers. Component 2: Psychosocial support and networking In addition to material supplies, psychosocial support is a key aspect of the project. Medical professionals in Ukraine in particular, who work under enormous psychological pressure, need help. The New Start project of the Mission Ukraine Charitable Foundation, in cooperation with Be an Angel e. V. and supported by the Else Kröner-Fresenius-Stiftung (EKFS), offers free psychological training for Ukrainian professionals working with war veterans and people close to the front line. The training will take place in Berlin from 13 to 20 December 2014. The aim is to use evidence-based approaches to strengthen the resilience of professionals and promote their ability to deal with stress. The Berlin-based organisation Zentrum Überleben will be organising a workshop as part of the project. In addition, a networking meeting will be organised in Berlin to discuss possible future cooperation and the establishment of a specialist network between doctors and psychologists from Kyiv and Berlin, with the aim of exchanging expertise and working together on strategies for coping with trauma. In the future, German-Ukrainian cooperation is to be expanded, particularly in the area of psychological war trauma management - an urgent task, as there are around 50,000 Ukrainian refugees living in Berlin alone as of 2024, many of whom are suffering from war trauma. This two-pronged project impressively demonstrates how humanitarian aid, medical support and psychosocial measures can work together to alleviate short-term hardship and create long-term structures. It is a sign that solidarity across national borders can save lives and open up new prospects.

title: Mental Health for Ukraine (MH4U)
long_description: The Mental Health for Ukraine project is a flagship Swiss engagement which strengthens the capacity and resilience of the mental health system in a context of growing demand and resource scarcity. Switzerland renews its multi-year commitment and pursues a tailored approach addressing acute mental health needs as a consequence of the conflict. The project contributes to the overall resilience of the Ukrainian people, aligns with government priorities and supports Ukraine's reform path.

title: Mental health project in Lebanon
long_description: This project considers the competence and psychological resilience of the professionals of the family guidance centers (FGCs) operating in the refugee camps in Lebanon, as well as the mental health and crisis resistance of the families living in the camps, in the current acute war situation in the Middle East and in the social instability of Lebanon. The project has two main objectives. In the first objective, the mental health work competence of the multidisciplinary employees of the FGCs run by the local partner in Lebanon is strengthened, as well as the psychological resilience to work in unstable conditions. Employees of FGCs are extensively trained in dealing with acute crises and traumas and in stress regulation. Managers of FGCs are trained in leadership skills. In addition, a permanent network of FGCs will be established, repair meetings, joint semester workshop updates to strengthen the working community to support employee well-being and psychological resilience. The second objective is to support the mental health and crisis resilience of families living in refugee camps in Lebanon. The project creates, pilots, implements, documents and stabilizes a community-level, psychosocial support action model implemented by social workers, in which the action model of psychosocial support is deployed from FGCs to communities and the promotion of community-level mental health and crisis resilience is implemented through many means: a team of 2-3 social workers will work in each of the five FGCs for the duration of the project, which implements low-threshold community activities, such as workshops, campaigns, child-parent activities, social media influence on locals, production of materials etc. With these multi-level measures, the psychological well-being and crisis resilience of people living in refugee camps in Lebanon who are at risk of being marginalized will be strengthened.

title: Mental illness and substance abuse in Uganda- the hidden pandemic
long_description: Mental and alcohol use disorders in Africa are seriously understudied and underfinanced but have a huge impact on the burden of disease, human suffering and progress towards goals of leaving no-one behind and Agenda 2030. During COVID-related lockdowns, mental distress has increased in high-income settings but primary data from Africa and appropriate interventions are lacking. However mental health is closely interlinked with school closures, lost life opportunities, poverty, food insecurity. This large population-based study in Uganda aims to analyse the occurrence of the most common mental disorders (depression, anxiety) and alcohol abuse, and interactions with poverty, age, gender, reproductive health (HIV), urbanicity, food insecurity and partner violence. We will validate tools on stigma against mental illness and care seeking, and, assess the influence of the pandemic on access to care and prevention for mental and alcohol use disorders. This 3-year project will use longitudinal data from a cohort of 11,000 individuals aged 13-80 years before, during and after the pandemic. Based on our results we will suggest new policy guidelines for health care and community interventions to mitigate the impact of mental disorders and change prevailing discriminatory views of mental health in general. We build on a strong collaboration between Karolinska and AMBSO research organisation in Uganda overall aiming to optimize capacity for operational research in low-income contexts.

long_description: The project 'Mothers for Peace and Ecology' supports and empowers refugee women, mothers, and their families from Ukraine, as well as their helpers in the Danube region. Focused on trauma-sensitive approaches, the project builds on three pillars: networking and exchange, capacity building and empowerment, along with promoting and developing initiatives for mother centres in Ukraine. It facilitates exchanges among participants, offers leadership and self-management training, and supports the establishment of mother centres to foster democracy and social diversity in the region. The project goals also include the development and adaptation of educational programs for women, mothers and their supporters. A focus is on supporting disadvantaged women, this also includes Roma woman with a refugee background, the promotion of ecologically oriented mother and family centres in the Danube region as well as to strengthen democratic awareness.

long_description: The aim of the project is to contribute to alleviating the difficult conditions experienced by the most vulnerable Ukrainian population in the Chernivtsi region, with a high presence of internally displaced persons and returnees. The specific objective is to improve the living conditions and wellbeing of 1,100 members of the population living in conditions of greater vulnerability (minors, women, elderly and people with disabilities), in the Chernivtsi region, through the provision of humanitarian aid and psychosocial support interventions. The project is divided into 3 activities: A1 Coordination, A2 Support for minors and parenting through Summer Camps, a theater workshop for minors and families, and an afterschool program in the period from September to December. A3 Multisector emergency aid to the most vulnerable Ukrainian population through recreational and occupational activities for the elderly, and the provision of blankets and vouchers for the purchase of medicines for displaced families, refugees and fragile residents, elderly, IDPs, women and people with disabilities.

long_description: The Mother Teresa House is a reception facility for sick and needy people, with particular attention to the disabled and those with mental illnesses. To date, the Mother Teresa House hosts around 70 people in situations of disability, poverty and total abandonment who come from very poor families who are unable to afford medical assistance and treatment. the number of users of the Mother Teresa House is constantly growing. Over time this has led to a situation of overloading of the structure with a lack of suitable spaces for reception and for the various support activities required by the type of users. Objective: to expand the Casa Madre Teresa, through the raising of an area of the existing building, to create a series of spaces to be used as bedrooms, services and spaces for educational and rehabilitation activities for the guests. Activities: start of lot 2 for the construction, in the rough, of the second part of the structure involved in the raising and expansion, start of the internal finishing activities of the entire area, both the one already built and currently unfinished and the one subject to the intervention referred to in the previous point, bringing the structure into operation to make it accessible and functional to the needs of the guests. title: Ngalu F?nifo - Community Mental Health in the Pacific
long_description: Ngalu F?nifo is a culturally driven pilot program designed to build capacity and capability of Pacific practitioners and communities in Tonga and Vanuatu, strengthen services across community, primary care and hospital settings, and support families to manage their own mental wellbeing. Being delivered by Pasifika Medical Association (PMA), the project will use Pacific Talanoa methodologies to co-design culturally-anchored models of care with pilot communities and clinical stakeholders. New models of care will better connect primary care, hospital practitioners and community providers, enabling them to better support individuals and families experiencing psychosocial stress and empower them to effectively care for their own mental wellbeing. PMA will also facilitate the development and delivery of training, using culturally-safe tools and develop national workforce and implementation plans to support Tonga and Vanuatu to roll-out the models of care nationally.

title: Norec, FK Norway, personnell exchange
long_description: Malawi, Zambia, Zimbabwe. Sports and recreation opportunities for children and youth are unfortunately not widespread or even prioritized in many countries of the world. In particular, there are considerable inequalities to access according to age and gender. This is the case in Africa as well, where the project aims to operate. Sports and recreation are considered an important part of child development, providing skills and behavioural frameworks that can accompany a person over its lifetime. In addition, participating in sports alleviates stress and impacts positively in mental health, including of course children. Even though Norway stands out as country with good enabling conditions for children in sports, there is nonetheless, room for improvement and the project has identified specific challenges for including women and young girls in sports. The project aims to create Safe, inclusive and sustainable sports environments for children and youth in all the partner countries. They expect to do this by:1-Engaging children and youth in sports activities2-Increase competence and opportunities for young coaches, and3-Capacity building for the implementing agencies

title: Promotion of Youth Employment and Resilience in Central America
long_description: ContextTwo out of three people in Guatemala, Honduras and El Salvador are under 30 years old. They are often affected by social exclusion and violence, with murder being the most common cause of death for ten to 19-year-olds.Social inequality and discrimination prevent access to vocational training and education, as well as to the labour market. Young people also experience multiple discrimination if they are women, belong to the LGBTIQ community or live with a disability. The situation is particularly problematic for young people in prison, especially men. Youth unemployment and a lack of opportunities pave the way for migration or recruitment by youth gangs.ObjectiveYoung people from neighbourhoods with high levels of violence have strengthened their psychosocial resilience and employability and have been able to develop skills that offer them alternatives to violence and irregular migration.ApproachThe project is working in four fields of activity:1. Employees of local and national organisations as well as youth peer educators receive training to promote the psychosocial resilience of young people.2. In particularly dangerous neighbourhoods, it is expanding non-formal vocational training opportunities for young people facing multiple discrimination.3. Companies that offer green or digital jobs are supported in developing successful practices so that young people can find a job.4. The project implements a youth-rights approach and assesses how youth participation can be integrated in development cooperation. Implementation is supported by a youth advisory board.The political partner is the General Secretariat of the Central American Integration System (SG-SICA), the implementing regional partner is the Secretariat for Social Integration of Central America (SISCA). The project promotes joint learning between neighbouring countries in Central America and advises regional actors in the Central American Integration System.

title: Protection of Orphans and Vulnerable children in Zimbabwe

title: Providing psychological and social assistance to internally displaced persons in western Ukraine

The main goal of the current project besides continuing of the given practices is building partnerships and networks among the organizations which are involved in the support of IDPs in the western region of Ukraine. Establishing communication between IDPs and host communities is crucial in preventing potential conflicts and fostering social relations. The project was implemented in the framework of Program of humanitarian, stabilization, reconstruction and economic assistance to Ukraine in 2023-2025 and was supported by financial donation of 5 milion CZK as an Aid in Place project in cooperation with Ukrainian NGO Kryla Nadiyi.

title: Provision of psychosocial support in children's hospitals in Kharkiv and Lviv oblasts in the context of war
long_description: The project 'Provision of psychosocial support in children's hospitals in Kharkiv and Lviv oblasts in the context of war' aims to strengthen mental health, psychosocial well-being, and resilience of the most vulnerable groups of the population in wartime Ukraine - children and youth hospitalized in medical facilities as a result of military attacks, but also short- and long-term illnesses, including incurable ones. The project does so by improving access to psychological support and psychosocial services in hospitals in Kharkiv and Lviv oblasts, and by improving the competencies of local professionals in psychosocial support topics crucial for strengthening the mental health of hospitalized children during the war. Thanks to the project we will provide psychosocial support in the form of group low-intensity activities and individual consultations for 2300 persons, mostly hospitalized children but also their parents. At the same time, we will create safe spaces for children in two hospitals to support their mental health further, and to decrease additional stress and trauma. In building local capacities, the project stems from the mhGAP concept, according to which, it is necessary to expand the knowledge and skills of health personnel on psychosocial support topics to improve the mental health of the population. Therefore, the project focuses on developing the competencies of medical personnel, with emphasis on students, psychologists and other medical professionals in hospitals through trainings, a workshop for practitioners, long-term supervision and development of referral systems to effectively and comprehensively capture the cases of hospitalized children who require closer support from a psychologist. In total, the project will improve access to psychosocial support for 3600 persons in two children's hospitals over the course of the year.

title: Psychological Support and Social Protection to Children
long_description: This project was developed and implemented with the support of the Special Representative of the OSCE Chair-in-Office – Project Co-ordinator in Ukraine. The project addresses current needs of children affected by war and aims at supporting national and local stakeholders by enhancing their/knowledge and skills to provide qualified social and psychological support to children. The project envisages support to the National Social Service of Ukraine (NSS) and its regional departments to have tools and capacities to co-ordinate, support and monitor provision of services by social service providers to children affected by war. The project also covers training and establishment of a pool of professionally trained social workers/and psychologists, as well as setting up comfort zones for children in social centres. These project interventions will help to reduce the impact of war-related trauma by providing timely psycho-social assistance to children. The project's direct beneficiaries are the NSS and its regional offices, social protection departments within oblast (regional) state administrations, and social centres in territorial communities. This project belongs to the Repository Programme 'OSCE Support Programme to Ukraine (SPU)' no. 1102458 and helps national and local/stakeholders to use enhanced tools and mechanisms to promote safety and security of communities and individuals.

title: Renovation of the courtyard of the Oasis d'Amour facility for the mentally ill in Bohicon.
long_description: In 2020 the Region financed the renovation of the kitchen, refectory and toilets for this center with €30,000.00. It is one of the 5 present in Benin, also in Burkina Faso, Togo and Ivory Coast there are Oasis d'Amour centers that take care of all the mentally ill abandoned on the streets and in the villages. The operators of the association La Communauté Saint Camille de Lellis , in addition to working in these centers, free the mentally ill who are segregated in the villages. In Africa even today, beliefs and superstitions are still very widespread and those suffering from psychiatric disorders are not treated as they are considered possessed . The project involves the arrangement of the courtyard, as during the rainy season the courtyard becomes impassable due to mud. New flooring is planned for a surface area of ??3,706 square metres. The surface will be leveled to allow rainwater to flow towards collection channels which will be built at the same time for a linear development of approximately 180 metres. The courtyard's foundation will be made of reinforced concrete and then concrete blocks will be laid to allow the passage of cars and ambulances. Beneficiaries: more than 200 patients and 84 collaborators.

With its faith-based member organizations of protestant background that are deeply anchored in the Swiss society, KoGe empowers disadvantaged people and provides access to food security, education and health. It also strengthens communities in peacebuilding and conflict transformation.

title: South-North embassy project: BRACE
long_description: The grant provided for the project BRACE (Building Resilience and Agency through Crafts and Expressive Arts) supports a series of therapeutic workshops for survivors of online sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, and commercial sexual exploitation. Focusing on pottery, photography, and painting, these three distinct workshops - each tailored to enhance survivor's coping skills and to promote emotional resiliency - allow PSN members to explore their emotions and to express themselves creatively. Thus, the project makes use of the transformative power of art. Additionally, it will also provide the PSN with an opportunity to enhance their project and grant management skills.

title: Spaces for the Psychological Rehabilitation of Children of Fallen Ukrainian Soldiers
long_description: A dedicated room will be created to provide psychological support and shared activities for children aged 6 to 18. It will offer a comfortable, safe space for those in need of psychological assistance, relaxation, rest, recovery, or simply a private conversation, as well as for trainings, education, and creative workshops. The room will be equipped with sensory tools and art therapy materials to help participants relax and strengthen their mental well-being.

title: Spreading 'Humour & Arts' across Palestinian Hospitals
long_description: The aim is to create a supportive environment in Palestinian hospitals in which children can exercise their rights to humor, play and creativity. To achieve this, the project is helping to systematically anchor Humor & Art as a recognized strategy for mental health and psychosocial well-being of children in Palestinian hospitals. (Contribution to SDG 3, SDG 4, SDG 5 and EU GAP II 10, 13).

title: Strengenthing the resilience of vulnerable households and war affected communities through community-driven recovery in Bucha Rajon
long_description: Residents of the project region are involved in the implementation of the municipal reconstruction plans. Civil society organisations that are developing and setting up community centres (hubs) in all project locations are being strengthened. These offer, among other things, equipped office workplaces (shared desk as in co-working spaces), childcare, meeting rooms for various events and counselling. Social cohesion among the direct target groups (including many internally displaced persons) in the project region is strengthened through social and cultural events such as business fairs, film screenings followed by discussions and sport events. These are organised and hosted on the initiative of local civil society actors, who are institutionally strengthened and supported by the project. Vulnerable people are enabled to apply for (non-)state support services. Selected individuals are retrained in new professions and placed in companies or supported in becoming self-employed, with the aim of strengthening the economic resilience of vulnerable households. One-off start-up funding is provided for this purpose. Exchange formats contribute to the transfer of knowledge for the further development of the Ukrainian participatory reconstruction agenda at oblast and national level. Gender equality and inclusion are applied as cross-cutting issues.

The Activity will also work to support community mental health initiatives to increase resilience in response to external disasters.

title: Strengthening Mental Health Awareness among Secondary School Students in Kenya
long_description: Stronger mental health for students means they can learn better and be more likely to realize the full potential of their abilities. These positive effects not only support the individual student, but also their larger community as they enter adulthood. Currently, there are increased cases of unrest among students in Kenyan schools that could probably be linked to mental health. More often, these have resulted to violence, massive destruction of school property and low educational outcomes. In meeting the social and emotional needs of students, School Based Support Initiatives (SBSI) are critical. Yet there is limited evidence on teachers' capacity to offer effective support to student towards strengthening capacity of teachers and students on mental health in selected secondary schools in Kenya. The project will adopt Participatory Action Research (PAR) approach and will be implemented over 24 months with eight (8) teachers, four (4) secondary school principals and students as peer mentors participating. The participants will be drawn from 4 schools, 1 school from each of the four selected Counties in the Lake Region Economic Bloc (Bungoma, Busia, Kisumu, and Kakamega) in Kenya. The objectives of the project are to: (a) conduct a baseline survey on the prevalence of mental health conditions among secondary school students, (b) develop a sensitization manual on mental health, and (c) identify the training needs and build capacity of teachers and students on mental health. The project is expected to improve staff attitude on mental health and skills to support students mental wellbeing.

The work, which takes place in a rented container in Kirikhan, supports over 300 women, children and young people every month through therapeutic counselling and creative activities.

title: Support for the National Institute of Mental Health's project to promote mental health (art therapy)

These services will be provided by Ukrainian artists who will be trained by Ukrainian psychotherapists. A secondary objective of this project is to provide job opportunities for artists or cultural sector workers who may have lost their jobs or were otherwise affected as a result of the war. The key output of this project will be the time devoted to art therapy assistance to convalescents (i.e., in simple terms, the number of art therapy sessions), including group therapy sessions. The outputs will also include the total number of people who will be provided with art therapy support and the number of participating artists - art therapy providers, or the number of participating artists who complete a specific art therapy course. The project is aimed at mental health promotion with an accent on post-traumatic stress disorder via artetherapy. Project is launched in cooperation with the National Institute of Mental Health and the total value of the project is 10 200 000 CZK.

At least 1,300 children have been injured as a result of the full-scale invasion (according to the General Prosecutor's Office of Ukraine, as of 15.05.2024), but even more have suffered psychological trauma. During the summer, the Foundation, together with its partners, aims to organise 4 camps (groups of 40-50 children) aimed at equipping children with skills and abilities to support themselves and others. During the project, children aged 9-17 will receive psychosocial support. These are children who have lost their parents, children who were forced to leave their homes, children from frontline areas, including those who have experienced deportation.

title: Supporting mental health of people with physical impairments in the Kingdom of Cambodia
long_description: The United Nations (UN) 2030 Agenda for sustainable development has made a pledge to 'leave no-one behind', a statement that has significant implications for the 15% of the world's population who live with a disability. People with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries face many barriers and experience poverty levels that are higher for this group than any other group without disabilities. Those who experience two or more disorders simultaneously e.g. a physical disorder and a mental health disorder, experience greater levels of disability and are among the poorest of the poor. This project will be conducted in Cambodia, a country that has experience some of the highers rates of disability in the world and aims to contribute knowledge regarding the prevalence and risk factors for mental health problems in people with physical disabilities. The project will develop, implement and evaluate a sustainable mental health screening and peer support program for individuals identified as being at risk of mental health problems.

title: Building Healthy Communities with the Dual Goal of Chronic Disease Prevention and Promoting Environmental Sustainability in Canada and Jamaica / Bâtir des communautés en bonne santé pour prévenir les maladies chroniques et promouvoir la durabilité environnementale au Canada et en Jamaïque
long_description: Heart attacks and strokes, known as cardiovascular diseases, are largely preventable and treatable. These chronic diseases often begin in childhood, through poor diet and low levels of outdoor active play. Taking steps to promote healthy eating and physical activity early in life can contribute to preventing these diseases in adulthood. However, we are seeing an increase in the prevalence of obesity, high blood pressure and diabetes in young people, especially in urban environments. This project aims to prevent the development of risk factors for future heart attacks and strokes in young people, and reduce the impact of producing and eating highly processed foods on the planet's climate, by encouraging consumption of locally and sustainably grown or harvested fruits and vegetables and safe outdoor play. The study will use data collected from national surveys and involve community engagement (including young people) to develop a multi-pronged intervention to improve their health in a way that is environmentally friendly. The interventions will be tested in cities in Canada and Jamaica. If the interventions prove successful, local governments and policymakers will be engaged to support a scaling strategy to implement similar interventions in additional communities. / Les crises cardiaques et les accidents vasculaires cérébraux, connus sous le nom de maladies cardiovasculaires, sont en grande partie évitables et traitables. title: Effects on cardiometabolic diseases in adolescents and young adults residing in food streets in Karachi, Pakistan: A mixed methods study
long_description: Programme: Early-Career Award. Description: Limited evidence exists from lower-middle-income countries (LMICs) on the contribution of the neighbourhood food environment towards cardiometabolic diseases (CMD). Pakistan witnesses 7% of myocardial infarctions in individuals <40\. Karachi, its largest city with 10 million people aged <25 years, is undergoing a rapid nutrition transition that led to the mushrooming of calorie-dense food shops and commercial 'Food Streets' (FS) within residential areas. FS has a variety of food shops in one place. Residents of FS may have a high intake of calorie-dense foods due to the constant exposure and accessibility of unhealthy food within walking distance. High intake of calorie-dense food can initiate physiologic dysregulation of lipids and sugar in the body, causing CMD (1). We propose a mixed methods study examining the relationship between the food environment, dietary intake, and CMD (prediabetes, diabetes, prehypertension, hypertension, and dyslipidemia) among 15-25-year individuals residing within a 2-kilometer radius of FS through mediation analysis. Semi-structured interviews of young residents, shopkeepers, regulatory authorities, and nutrition experts will explore the barriers and facilitators to enabling a healthy eating environment. The key outcome of my work, driven by study findings, will be the co-creation of an intervention package with participants, to foster a healthy food environment.

Partner countries (PNG, Malaysia, Timor-Leste, Solomon Islands, Vanuatu, Tuvalu, Fiji and Nauru) are tiered according to readiness, gaps and priorities. title: Evaluating and bringing to scale alternative food networks to address diabetes mellitus and hypertension in Ecuador / Évaluation et mise à l'échelle de réseaux d'alimentation alternatifs afin de lutter contre le diabète sucré et l'hypertension en Équateur
long_description: In Ecuador, rural people, and particularly rural Indigenous people, are disproportionately affected by nutrient inadequacies, obesity, and overweight. This double burden of malnutrition magnifies their risk of developing diet-related chronic diseases such as diabetes mellitus and hypertension. In parallel, many rural Indigenous people in Ecuador have organized around alternative food networks, such as farmers' markets, to seek more sustainable livelihoods. Alternative food networks promote food literacy (understanding the impact of food choices on one's health, the environment, and the economy), favour the consumption of fruits, vegetables, and whole grains, and put income into women's hands. These benefits have been associated with better nutrition and a reduced risk of diet-related chronic disease. This project aims to evaluate specific alternative food network approaches to measure their contribution to diabetes and hypertension prevention. The research will leverage the most effective approaches for a stronger and broader positive impact. Findings will be shared among an estimated 132 Ecuadorian alternative food networks, positioning them to streamline research findings into practice. Overall, the project is expected to provide strategic and practical guidance for integrating health-sensitive attributes into the regular practices of alternative food networks as they continue to multiply and evolve in Ecuador and elsewhere. / En Équateur, les populations rurales, et en particulier les populations autochtones rurales, sont touchées de manière disproportionnée par les carences en nutriments, l'obésité et la surcharge pondérale. Parallèlement, de nombreux peuples autochtones ruraux équatoriens, à la recherche de modes d'existence plus durables, se sont organisés autour d'autres réseaux alimentaires alternatifs tels que les marchés de producteurs.
